_about: Per-jurisdiction interest, fee-shifting and deficiency rules for commercial contract claims, researched 2026-09-26 from statute and rule text (citations and URLs on each entry). States N-W were read twice independently; A-M once. resolutions[] records how disagreements were settled. ratePct is the percent rate for 2026 where fixed or computed; null where discretionary or formula-only.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 3 percentage points above the 12th Federal Reserve District discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year the judgment is entered (6.75% for judgments entered in 2026 per Alaska Court System form ADM-505). Same rate for pre- and post-judgment; fixed for the life of the judgment.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Earlier of service of process or defendant's receipt of written notice of the claim, unless the parties agreed otherwise (AS 09.30.070(b)); court form ADM-505 describes contract claims as accruing when the contract was first breached

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same as prejudgment: 12th District Fed discount rate on Jan 2 of year of entry + 3 points; a judgment on a written contract specifying an interest rate (not exceeding the legal rate for that contract type) bears the contract rate if the rate is set out in the judgment.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: AS 09.30.070(a); Alaska Court System form ADM-505 (1/26)

feeShifting.citation: Alaska R. Civ. P. 82(a)-(b) (prevailing party in any civil case 'shall be awarded' fees per schedule, 'except as otherwise provided by law or agreed to by the parties'): money judgment, contested with trial 20% of first $25,000 + 10% of excess; contested without trial 18%/8%/6%/2% tiers (first $25k / next $75k / next $400k / over $500k); non-contested 10%/3%/2%/1%; no money judgment 30% (trial) or 20% (no trial) of reasonable actual fees

deficiency.citation: AS 34.20.100 (no deficiency against maker, surety or guarantor after trustee's sale under a deed of trust); AS 09.45.170-.180 (judicial foreclosure judgment determines personal liability; deficiency between judgment and sale price enforceable by execution)

AK.notes: Alaska is a loser-pays (English rule) state by court rule, not statute; a contractual fee clause displaces the Rule 82 schedule ('agreed to by the parties'). No statute makes a one-sided clause reciprocal. Deficiency: nonjudicial deed-of-trust sale bars any deficiency, including against guarantors; lender must foreclose judicially to preserve one. No FMV-offset statute located for judicial foreclosure. No deficiency-specific deadline verified (timeLimit null). Prejudgment accrual under 09.30.070(b) is statute-worded around notice of injury; for contract claims courts generally run it from breach, as the court's own form states.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: breach (the day the money should have been paid) per Ala. Code 8-8-8
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Ala. Code §§ 8-8-8 (contracts bear interest from the day payment was due), 8-8-1 (legal rate $6 per $100 per year absent written contract; written contract may set up to 8% under this section, subject to other statutes)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgments based on a contract action bear interest from the day of the cause of action at the rate stated in the contract; all other judgments 7.5% per annum (judgments entered on/after Sept. 1, 2011).

deficiency.citation: No anti-deficiency statute; nonjudicial power-of-sale foreclosure under Ala. Code § 35-10-11 et seq.; Mt. Carmel Estates, Inc. v. Regions Bank, 853 So. 2d 160 (Ala. 2002) (mortgagee's credit bid must be made in good faith; a bid shockingly below fair market value can be challenged)

AL.notes: Prejudgment: 8-8-8 makes interest run from the date payment was due; the 6% legal rate of 8-8-1 applies absent a contract rate (8-8-1's 8% written-contract cap is the historic usury ceiling, largely superseded for commercial loans by other statutes; a stated lease/note rate governs). Fees: Alabama follows the American rule; contractual fee clauses are enforced as written, with no statute making a one-sided clause reciprocal and no general contract fee statute. Deficiency: no statute bars or FMV-caps a commercial deficiency; protection is case law on grossly inadequate credit bids (Mt. Carmel). Deficiency URL is a secondary summary (Nolo), not statute text. No deficiency-specific filing deadline; the limitations period on the underlying note/guaranty governs (not separately verified here, so timeLimit left null).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: In an action on a contract: the greater of the contract rate or the Federal Reserve primary credit rate in effect on the date judgment is entered + 2%; capped at the maximum under Ark. Const. amend. 89. Where the contract states no rate, 4-57-101(d) sets 6% as the contract rate, so the formula (primary credit + 2) governs if higher.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Statute is silent ('if appropriate under the facts of the case'); Arkansas case law allows prejudgment interest where damages are ascertainable by fixed standard at the time of the loss/breach, running from that date

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Contract actions: greater of contract rate or Fed primary credit rate on date of judgment + 2%; other actions: primary credit + 2%; capped by Ark. Const. amend. 89.

feeShifting.citation: Ark. Code Ann. § 16-22-308 (in actions on open account, promissory note, negotiable instrument, contract for goods or services, or breach of contract, the prevailing party MAY be allowed a reasonable fee, 'unless otherwise provided by law or the contract'); discretionary, available to either side

deficiency.timeLimit: 12 months after a sale under the Statutory Foreclosure Act (nonjudicial)
deficiency.citation: Ark. Code Ann. § 18-50-112 (deficiency action within 12 months of statutory-foreclosure sale; plaintiff must prove FMV; judgment limited to the lesser of debt minus FMV or debt minus sale price)

AR.notes: Pre-2013 the contract judgment rate was the greater of contract rate or 10%; now floats with the Fed primary credit rate at entry, so rate is null (compute primary credit + 2, compared with contract rate). Fee statute 16-22-308 is discretionary and is displaced if the contract provides otherwise; it is not a reciprocity statute but applies to either prevailing side. Deficiency rule verified here is for nonjudicial statutory foreclosure; judicial foreclosure deficiency is also permitted in Arkansas but its statutory FMV treatment was not verified.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the liquidated obligation became due (statute does not specify; case law runs it from when the sum was due/liquidated)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: A.R.S. § 44-1201(A)(2) (10% a year on any loan, indebtedness or other obligation unless a different rate is contracted for in writing), (D)(1) (no prejudgment interest on unliquidated damages), (F) (prejudgment interest, if awarded, at the rate in subsection A or B)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Lesser of 10% or prime rate (Fed H.15) + 1%, fixed at the rate in effect on the date of judgment and stated in the judgment; a judgment on a written agreement bearing a lawful interest rate carries the agreement's rate.

feeShifting.citation: A.R.S. § 12-341.01(A)-(C) (in any contested action arising out of contract, court MAY award the successful party reasonable fees; discretionary; award may not exceed fees actually paid or agreed; rejected written settlement offer shifts successful-party status; does not displace contractual fee provisions)

deficiency.timeLimit: 90 days after trustee's sale (deed of trust); for judicial foreclosure, FMV application within 30 days after sheriff's sale
deficiency.citation: A.R.S. § 33-814(A)-(D), (G) (deficiency after trustee's sale = debt less greater of FMV or sale price; action within 90 days or sale proceeds deemed full satisfaction; residential 2.5-acre 1-2 family dwelling exemption not applicable to commercial); § 12-1566(B)-(C) (judicial foreclosure: credit for greater of FMV or sheriff's sale price)

AZ.notes: Statute sets the 10% default for liquidated obligations; whether a pre-judgment award on a contract claim uses 10% under (A)(2) or the prime+1 formula under (B) has been litigated; the prevailing reading applies (A)(2)'s 10% to indebtedness/obligations. A written contract rate controls both pre- and post-judgment. Postjudgment rate field null because it floats with prime at entry; compute as min(10, prime+1). Fees under 12-341.01 are discretionary (court weighs Associated Indemnity v. Warner factors) and are not a reciprocity statute, but in practice let either side recover in a contract action. Deficiency: 33-814(F) lets a deed of trust expressly waive deficiency; 12-1566(E) lets a guarantor's obligation be enforced independently but guarantor still gets the FMV credit.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Liquidated (certain) damages: from the day the right to recover vested, i.e., when payment was due (Civ. Code 3287(a)); unliquidated contract damages: in court's discretion, no earlier than the filing date (3287(b))
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Cal. Civ. Code §§ 3287(a)-(b), 3289(a)-(b) (contract rate remains chargeable after breach; if contract made after 1/1/1986 stipulates no rate, 10% per annum after breach; 'contract' in 3289(b) excludes a note secured by a deed of trust on real property)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 10% per annum on unsatisfied principal of a money judgment (5% applies only to certain consumer medical/personal-debt judgments against natural persons, not commercial claims).

feeShifting.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1717(a)-(b) (a contract fee clause favoring one party or the prevailing party entitles whichever party prevails on the contract to reasonable fees; not waivable; prevailing party = party recovering greater relief; no prevailing party on voluntary dismissal/settlement)

deficiency.allowed: judicial foreclosure only (as to the borrower)
deficiency.timeLimit: Judicial: deficiency application within 3 months of the foreclosure sale (CCP 726(b)). After a power-of-sale (nonjudicial) sale, no deficiency is owed at all by the borrower (CCP 580d); CCP 580a (FMV cap, action within 3 months) governs money judgments after power-of-sale sales in the limited cases 580d does not reach, such as some guarantor or other-collateral situations.
deficiency.citation: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §§ 580d (no deficiency after sale under power of sale; guarantor/surety liability preserved), 580a (FMV limit for post-power-of-sale money judgments), 726 (one-action rule; judicial-foreclosure deficiency limited to debt less fair value, application within 3 months)

CA.notes: 3289(b)'s 10% default does not apply to a note secured by a deed of trust; courts apply the 7% constitutional legal rate (Cal. Const. art. XV, § 1) to such notes absent a contract rate (not separately fetched here). Unliquidated contract claims get discretionary prejudgment interest from no earlier than filing. California's one-action rule (CCP 726) and anti-deficiency statutes apply to commercial loans too; 580b (purchase-money) mostly residential. Guarantor liability is preserved by 580d(b), subject to Civ. Code 2856 waivers.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 8% per annum compounded annually; alternatively, at claimant's election under 5-12-102(1)(a), the gain or benefit realized by the withholding party
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the money became due or was wrongfully withheld (5-12-102(1)(b), (2)); available even if the amount was unliquidated (5-12-102(3)); runs to payment or entry of judgment
prejudgmentInterest.citation: C.R.S. § 5-12-102(1)-(3) (applies 'when there is no agreement as to the rate')

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Contract/instrument rate if it provides for interest until paid (variable rate: rate in effect on date of judgment); otherwise 8% compounded annually. If the judgment debtor appeals and no written rate agreement exists, the rate is the Secretary of State's annually certified rate (Kansas City Fed discount rate + 2, rounded to nearest full percent, floor 8%), compounded annually, from original entry (5-12-106).

feeShifting.citation: C.R.S. § 13-40-123 (prevailing party in a forcible entry and detainer (eviction/possession) action recovers reasonable fees; commercial parties regardless of a lease clause; residential parties only if the agreement provides for fees) -- limited to FED actions, not a general contract fee statute

deficiency.citation: C.R.S. § 38-38-106(6) (foreclosing holder must bid at least its good-faith estimate of FMV less senior liens, taxes and holding/sale costs, capped at total debt; failure is a defense for any person sued on a deficiency)

CO.notes: Colorado prejudgment interest is statutory and compounds annually. Fees: no reciprocity statute and no general contract-fee statute; contractual fee clauses enforced as written. 13-40-123 gives fees to the prevailing party in eviction (FED) actions, which in a commercial lease case can include rent damages awarded in that action. Deficiency: permitted after public-trustee foreclosure; FMV protection operates through the lender's good-faith bid requirement (a defense reducing the deficiency), not a court FMV hearing. No deficiency-specific filing deadline located (timeLimit null; the note/guaranty limitations period governs).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Up to 10% a year ('at the rate of ten per cent a year, and no more, may be recovered'); award and rate within the cap are in the trial court's discretion and require a wrongful detention of money
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the money 'becomes payable' (date the debt was due/wrongfully detained)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 37-3a(a); see also § 52-192a (offer of compromise: 8% from complaint filing if plaintiff's rejected offer is met or beaten)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Discretionary, up to 10% a year under the same statute (37-3a) as damages for detention of money after judgment; contract rate may apply where the instrument provides for it.

feeShifting.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-150bb makes a one-sided fee clause reciprocal only in contracts or leases to which a CONSUMER is a party -- not applicable to commercial leases or loans between businesses

deficiency.timeLimit: Motion within 30 days after the time limited for redemption expires (strict foreclosure)
deficiency.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 49-14(a) (court values the property at an evidentiary hearing and enters deficiency for the difference between that valuation and plaintiff's claim; further action on the debt recovers only that amount)

CT.notes: Connecticut prejudgment interest under 37-3a is discretionary (cap 10%), not automatic; rate field shows the cap. Where the note/lease provides a contract rate, the contract rate is recovered as contract damages rather than 37-3a interest. No reciprocal fee statute for commercial contracts and no general contract fee statute (42-150bb is consumer-only). Deficiency rule verified for strict foreclosure (49-14); foreclosure by sale has a separate provision (49-28) not fetched here.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Liquidated debt: from the time the debt was due and payable (15-108). Unliquidated contract damages: interest may be included as an element of damages in the factfinder's discretion (15-109).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: D.C. Code §§ 15-108 (judgment on a liquidated debt includes interest from when due, at the contract rate if any), 28-3302(a) (legal rate 6% absent expressed contract), 15-109 (contract damages: discretionary interest as element of damages)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Contract rate if fixed by contract; otherwise 70% of the IRS underpayment rate under 26 U.S.C. 6621, rounded to the nearest full percent (exactly one-half rounds up); court may lower for good cause or debtor's good-faith inability to pay. Judgments against the District: not more than 4%.

deficiency.citation: D.C. Code § 42-816 (in judicial foreclosure by sale, court may enter an in personam decree for the residue of the mortgage debt after applying net sale proceeds, where the complainant could sue for that residue); deficiency also recoverable by action on the note after nonjudicial sale

DC.notes: DC follows the American rule; contractual fee clauses are enforced as written and no statute makes a one-sided clause reciprocal or awards fees on contract claims generally (none located). Postjudgment rate floats with the IRS underpayment rate (the D.C. Superior Court posts the current figure), so rate is null. Deficiency: no anti-deficiency or FMV-credit statute located for commercial property; timeLimit null (note/guaranty limitations period governs).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Legal rate = Federal Reserve discount rate (including any surcharge) + 5%, measured 'as of the time from which interest is due' (i.e., the breach/due date, not the judgment date). Applies only where there is no expressed contract rate.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: The time from which interest is due (breach / payment due date)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: From the date of judgment on agreements governed by 2301(a): the LESSER of the contract rate or Federal Reserve discount rate (incl. surcharge) + 5%.

feeShifting.citation: 10 Del. C. § 3912 (in actions to enforce a note, bond, mortgage, invoice or other written instrument that expressly provides for fees, a plaintiff who recovers judgment may recover reasonable counsel fees not exceeding 20% of principal and interest adjudged) -- a cap on plaintiffs' contractual fees, not a reciprocity or general fee statute

deficiency.citation: No anti-deficiency statute; foreclosure by scire facias sur mortgage (10 Del. C. ch. 49, subch. XI) is in rem on the mortgage, so a deficiency requires an action on the note/bond; Girard Trust Bank v. Castle Apartments, Inc., 379 A.2d 1144 (Del. Super. 1977) (court may set aside a sale or limit deficiency where the price is grossly inadequate)

DE.notes: Delaware awards prejudgment interest on contract claims as of right under case law, at the 2301(a) legal rate fixed as of the date interest became due; Court of Chancery has discretion to compound. The discount rate at the relevant due date must be looked up (rate null). 2301(c) removes usury limits for loans over $100,000 not secured by the borrower's principal residence, so any agreed commercial rate controls. Fees: no reciprocity or general fee statute; 3912's 20% cap applies to fee recovery in suits on written instruments. Deficiency: no FMV-credit statute; relief for grossly inadequate price is case law (Girard Trust). Deficiency URL is the statute chapter on scire facias; the Girard Trust point comes from a secondary summary (Nolo).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Statutory rate set quarterly by the Chief Financial Officer under s. 55.03(1): 12-month average of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York discount rate + 400 basis points. Prejudgment interest uses the rate(s) in effect over the accrual period. Published rates: 2025 Q1 9.38, Q2 9.15, Q3 8.90, Q4 8.65; 2026 Q1 8.44, Q2 8.25, Q3 8.06, Q4 (from Oct. 1, 2026) 7.87.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date of loss / date payment was due on a liquidated claim (Argonaut Ins. Co. v. May Plumbing Co., 474 So. 2d 212 (Fla. 1985), case law, not statute)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Fla. Stat. § 55.03(1) ('Nothing contained herein shall affect a rate of interest established by written contract or obligation'); Argonaut Ins. Co. v. May Plumbing Co., 474 So. 2d 212 (Fla. 1985)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: CFO quarterly rate in effect when judgment is obtained (NY Fed discount rate 12-month average + 4%), stated on the judgment's face and adjusted each January 1 to the then-current rate until paid; a written contract rate is unaffected. Current: 8.06% (Jul. 1, 2026 quarter); 7.87% from Oct. 1, 2026.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Fla. Stat. § 55.03(1)-(3); Florida CFO judgment interest rate table

feeShifting.citation: Fla. Stat. § 57.105(7) (if a contract gives fees to a party who must act to enforce it, the court may also allow reasonable fees to the other party when it prevails in any action with respect to the contract; contracts on/after Oct. 1, 1988)

deficiency.citation: Fla. Stat. § 702.06 (deficiency decree within the court's sound discretion; FMV cap applies only to owner-occupied residential property; lender may alternatively sue at common law for the deficiency unless the foreclosure court already granted or denied it)

FL.notes: Prejudgment interest on liquidated contract damages is a matter of right under Argonaut (case law), at the 55.03 statutory rate(s). Fee reciprocity under 57.105(7) is mandatory in effect ('may' has been read to require reciprocal treatment). No general contract fee statute. Deficiency: judicial foreclosure; court has equitable discretion (courts commonly consider FMV) but the statutory FMV cap is residential-only, so fmvLimit=false for commercial. The 1-year deficiency limitations period in s. 95.11(5)(h) is limited to 1-4 family residential property (not fetched here); commercial deficiency claims fall under the general written-contract period, so timeLimit left null.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Liquidated demands: from the time the party became liable to pay (or from demand if payable on demand)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: O.C.G.A. §§ 7-4-15 (liquidated demands bear interest from when due), 7-4-2(a)(1)(A) (legal rate 7% simple where no rate is set by written contract); § 7-4-16 (commercial accounts for goods/services: up to 1.5%/month after 30 days past due)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate (Fed H.15) on the day judgment is entered + 3%; if the judgment is on a written contract/obligation specifying a rate, the contract rate. Applies automatically.

feeShifting.citation: O.C.G.A. § 13-1-11 (fee clauses in notes or other evidence of indebtedness enforceable only after 10-day post-maturity notice; a stated percentage is capped at 15% of principal+interest; 'reasonable fees' without a percentage = 15% of the first $500 + 10% of the excess; debtor may seek reasonableness review if the formula yields >$20,000); separately O.C.G.A. § 13-6-11 allows fees as expenses of litigation for bad faith, stubborn litigiousness or unnecessary trouble (not fetched here)

deficiency.timeLimit: Report the nonjudicial sale to the superior court for confirmation within 30 days after the sale; without a confirmation order no deficiency judgment may be obtained
deficiency.citation: O.C.G.A. § 44-14-161 (court must find the property brought its true market value before confirming; debtor gets 5 days' notice; court may order resale)

GA.notes: Georgia is unusual on fees: 13-1-11 is a statutory formula that applies whenever a note or other 'evidence of indebtedness' contains a fee clause (Georgia courts have applied it to commercial leases and guaranties; that case law was not separately verified here), and it is one-sided (creditor only); there is no reciprocity statute. Confirmation under 44-14-161 is a precondition to a deficiency against the debtor; if the sale price is below true market value confirmation is denied (no partial FMV credit), barring the deficiency unless resale is ordered. Guarantors' ability to waive confirmation is a case-law issue (not verified here). 7-4-16's 1.5%/month applies to commercial accounts for goods or services, not ordinarily to rent or loan principal.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Court designates the commencement date; for breach of contract it may be as early as the date of breach (636-16). Under 478-2, money due on a written instrument bears interest after it becomes due; settlement of accounts from when the balance is ascertained; open account 60 days after last item.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. §§ 478-2 (10% a year absent an express written contract rate), 636-16 (court sets commencement date; breach date is earliest for contract claims)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 10% a year, 'and no more', on any civil judgment.

feeShifting.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 607-14 (in all actions in the nature of assumpsit and on written contracts providing for fees, the LOSING party pays the prevailing party's reasonable fees, capped at 25% of the judgment (or the lower contract percentage); assessed on the amount sued for if the defendant prevails)

deficiency.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 667-38 (deficiency barred only against an owner-occupant after nonjudicial foreclosure of residential property); no statutory bar for commercial property

HI.notes: Hawaii prejudgment interest under 636-16 is discretionary as to the start date (the award itself is discretionary, typically to compensate for delay); rate is 478-2's 10% unless a written contract fixes another. 607-14 is both a general contract/assumpsit fee statute and effectively reciprocal (prevailing party, plaintiff or defendant), capped at 25% of the judgment or amount sued for. Deficiency: commercial deficiency not statutorily barred; no FMV-credit statute or deficiency-specific deadline located.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Money due by express contract / after it becomes due; settled accounts from when balance ascertained; open accounts 6 months after last item
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Iowa Code § 535.2(1) (5% 'unless the parties shall agree in writing' to another lawful rate; 535.2(2) lets business/real-estate borrowers agree to any rate)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: One-year Treasury constant maturity (Fed H.15 report settled immediately before the judgment date) + 2%, computed daily; if the judgment is on a contract fixing a rate, the contract rate (not above the 535.2 maximum). State court administrator circulates the rate monthly.

feeShifting.citation: Iowa Code §§ 625.22(1) (when judgment is recovered on a written contract containing a fee agreement, court shall tax a reasonable fee), 625.24 (attorney affidavit of no fee-splitting required), 625.25 (defendant must have had opportunity to pay before suit) -- enforces contract clauses in favor of the recovering party; not a reciprocity statute

deficiency.timeLimit: No statutory bar for commercial property; the 2-year post-judgment voiding rule of 615.1 applies only to agricultural property and owner-occupied 1-2 family dwellings
deficiency.citation: Iowa Code § 615.1 (foreclosure judgments on agricultural or owner-occupied 1-2 family residential property become void 2 years after entry; commercial property not covered)

IA.notes: Prejudgment interest on a liquidated contract claim runs at the 5% legal rate from the due date absent a written rate; 668.13's commencement-of-action rule is for tort-chapter actions. Postjudgment rate floats with the 1-year Treasury at judgment (rate null). Iowa fee statute 625.22 is one-directional (the party recovering judgment on a contract with a fee clause) and no reciprocity statute for commercial contracts was located. Deficiency: judicial foreclosure allowed for commercial property with no FMV-credit statute located.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When money becomes due (money due by express contract / after it becomes due); settlement of mutual accounts from when balance ascertained; open accounts 3 months after last item
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Idaho Code § 28-22-104(1) (12% a year when there is no express written contract fixing a different rate)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 5% + base rate (weekly average 1-year constant-maturity Treasury yield, second week of June, rounded up to nearest 1/8%), announced by the State Treasurer each July 1 and applying to judgments entered in the following 12 months; 365-day year. 8.875% for judgments entered July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027 (9.125% for July 1, 2025-June 30, 2026).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Idaho Code § 28-22-104(2); Idaho State Treasurer, Legal Rate of Interest

feeShifting.citation: Idaho Code § 12-120(3) (in any civil action to recover on an open account, note, guaranty, contract for goods or services, or ANY COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION -- all transactions except personal/household -- the prevailing party SHALL be allowed a reasonable fee); § 12-120(1) (claims pleaded at $35,000 or less, with 10-day pre-suit written demand)

deficiency.timeLimit: Within 3 months after a trustee's sale under a deed of trust
deficiency.citation: Idaho Code §§ 45-1512 (deed of trust: action within 3 months; judgment limited to debt minus FMV, and never more than debt minus sale price), 6-108 (judicial mortgage foreclosure: deficiency limited to debt plus costs minus reasonable value found by the court)

ID.notes: Idaho's 12-120(3) makes fee-shifting mandatory to the prevailing party (plaintiff or defendant) in every commercial transaction case, which covers commercial leases and loans; this functions as a general, bilateral contract fee statute even without a lease clause. Prejudgment 12% is the statutory legal rate for liquidated sums; a written contract rate controls.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When money becomes due on a bond, bill, note or other instrument of writing (a written lease qualifies as an instrument of writing); settled accounts from the day the balance is ascertained; also money withheld by unreasonable and vexatious delay
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 815 ILCS 205/2 (Interest Act)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 9% per annum from the date of judgment until satisfied (6% against government units; 5% for consumer-debt judgments of $25,000 or less against natural persons, not applicable to commercial claims); interest on an award/verdict runs from the verdict to entry of judgment at the same rate.

deficiency.timeLimit: Entered in the order confirming the foreclosure sale, if requested in the complaint and personal service was obtained on the obligor
deficiency.citation: 735 ILCS 5/15-1508(e) (personal deficiency judgment for balance over sale proceeds, entered with the order confirming sale)

IL.notes: Illinois Interest Act 5% applies absent a contract rate; whether a claim qualifies (written instrument, liquidated/ascertainable) is case law. Fees: American rule; no reciprocity statute for commercial contracts and no general contract fee statute located (contract fee clauses enforced as written). Deficiency: judicial foreclosure; deficiency is computed from sale proceeds, with no statutory FMV credit (court can refuse to confirm a sale whose terms are unconscionable under 15-1508(b), not fetched here). A lender can also sue separately on the note/guaranty.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Written instrument with no stated rate: from the date of settlement (when the sum became due); account stated / money had and received: from the date an itemized bill was rendered and payment demanded (24-4.6-1-103). Common-law prejudgment interest on contract claims is allowed when damages are ascertainable by fixed rules as of the breach.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Ind. Code §§ 24-4.6-1-102 (8% absent agreed rate), 24-4.6-1-103 (8% accrual rules for written instruments and accounts)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: From the verdict/finding until satisfied: the rate in the original contract sued upon but not more than 8%; 8% if no contract rate.

deficiency.timeLimit: Personal judgment entered with the judgment of foreclosure (judicial foreclosure)
deficiency.citation: Ind. Code § 32-30-10-5 (court shall give personal judgment against any party liable on the secured debt and order the mortgaged premises sold first)

IN.notes: Indiana caps postjudgment interest at 8% even where the contract rate is higher. Fees: American rule; no reciprocal or general contract fee statute located for commercial contracts (contract fee clauses enforced as written). Deficiency: judicial foreclosure with personal judgment; no FMV-credit statute; the deficiency can be lost if the borrower waives the redemption waiting period under 32-29-7-5 with the lender's agreement (secondary source, not fetched).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When money becomes due (liquidated); settled accounts from the day the balance is ascertained; also money withheld by unreasonable and vexatious delay
prejudgmentInterest.citation: K.S.A. § 16-201(a) (10% when no other rate is agreed); § 16-205(a) (a contract rate continues until full payment)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment on a contract specifying a rate: the contract rate, stated in the judgment (16-205(a)). Otherwise New York Fed discount rate as of July 1 + 4 points, reset every July 1 for ALL outstanding judgments (not fixed at entry), published by the Secretary of State: 7.75% for July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027 (8.25% for 2025-26). Limited-actions (small) judgments: 12%.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: K.S.A. §§ 16-204(e), 16-205(a); Kansas Secretary of State finance rates

feeShifting.citation: K.S.A. § 58-2312 (a note, mortgage or other credit agreement may provide for reasonable collection costs including attorney fees, excluding salaried-employee costs and not both attorney and collection-agency fees) -- validates creditor fee clauses; not reciprocal

deficiency.citation: Judicial foreclosure with personal judgment; K.S.A. § 60-2414 (redemption; for non-agricultural, non-owner-occupied property the mortgage may waive or shorten redemption) -- no anti-deficiency or FMV-credit statute located

KS.notes: Kansas prejudgment interest on liquidated sums is 10% (tort actions filed after July 1, 2023 use 16-204 rate minus 2, not relevant to contract). Postjudgment floating rate resets annually for existing judgments. No reciprocal or general contract fee statute for commercial claims located; contract clauses enforced (58-2312 for credit agreements). Deficiency: allowed after judicial foreclosure; per secondary sources a court can refuse to confirm a sale at a substantially inadequate bid and no deficiency is available when service was by publication only (not verified in statute text).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: After default (360.010(4): written contract with no stated rate earns the legal rate 'after default and until judgment')
prejudgmentInterest.citation: KRS § 360.010(1), (3), (4) (legal rate 8%; a written contract rate applies after default until judgment and becomes the judgment rate under 360.040(3); variable contract rates keep adjusting)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 6% compounded annually from entry (judgments entered on/after June 29, 2017), including on the prejudgment-interest component; a judgment on a contract, note or other written obligation bears the rate established in that instrument; court may set less than 6% on unliquidated-damages judgments after a hearing.

feeShifting.citation: KRS § 411.195 (written provisions creating a debt or real-property lien that require the debtor to pay the creditor's reasonable fees on default are enforceable, only to the extent actually paid or agreed to be paid; not for salaried employees) -- one-directional, validates creditor clauses

deficiency.citation: KRS §§ 426.525 (nonjudicial foreclosure forbidden -- judicial sale required), 426.530(1) (if the judicial sale brings less than 2/3 of appraised value, defendant may redeem within 6 months); deficiency judgment on the debt is otherwise available

KY.notes: Kentucky allows prejudgment interest on liquidated claims as a matter of right (case law) at the 8% legal rate or the contract rate; unliquidated claims are discretionary. Postjudgment 6% compounds annually. No reciprocity or general contract fee statute; 411.195 enforces creditor-side fee clauses. Deficiency: judicial foreclosure only; the 2/3-of-appraisal rule creates a redemption right rather than an FMV credit, so fmvLimit=false; no deficiency-specific deadline located.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Legal (judicial) interest per R.S. 9:3500(B)(1) and 13:4202(B): Fed discount rate on the first business day of October + 3.25 points, effective for the following calendar year and applied year by year over the accrual period. Published rates: 2025 = 8.25%, 2026 = 7.50%.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time the sum was due (La. Civ. Code art. 2000), without proof of loss

postjudgmentInterest.formula: No separate postjudgment rate: the same judicial interest rate (13:4202) continues to accrue until paid, changing each calendar year (2026: 7.50%); a conventional (contract) rate continues if agreed.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: La. R.S. 13:4202(B); Louisiana Office of Financial Institutions judicial interest rate table

feeShifting.citation: La. Civ. Code art. 2000 (obligee recovers attorney fees only where a written contract expressly makes the obligor liable in a fixed or determinable amount); La. R.S. 9:2781 (open accounts: claimant recovers reasonable fees if debtor fails to pay within 30 days after written demand)

deficiency.allowed: only if the property was sold with appraisement
deficiency.citation: La. R.S. 13:4106 (if the creditor uses the debtor's waiver of appraisement and the judicial sale proceeds are insufficient, the personal debt is fully discharged -- no deficiency, subject to exceptions 'provided by law' such as R.S. 13:4107)

LA.notes: Louisiana civil-law system: interest on a money obligation is 'damages for delay' running from the due date at the contract rate or the annually reset judicial rate; the same judicial rate continues after judgment, so pre- and post-judgment rates are one schedule. Conventional (contract) interest cap of 12% in 9:3500(C) has broad commercial exceptions (not analyzed). Fees: no reciprocity or general contract statute; contract fee clauses enforced as written (art. 2000); 9:2781 open-account fees are creditor-side. Deficiency: executory-process sale with appraisal (sale must bring at least two-thirds of appraised value at first offering under CCP rules, not fetched) preserves a deficiency; sale without appraisal extinguishes it. Exceptions in 13:4107 not fetched.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date of breach or demand; if not established, date the action was commenced. Added by the clerk automatically (mandatory).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 231, § 6C (contract rate if established, otherwise 12% per annum)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: From entry of judgment at the same annual rate as the prejudgment interest in the award (i.e., the contract rate if established, otherwise 12%).

deficiency.timeLimit: Deficiency action within 2 years after the foreclosure sale (or 2 years after principal accrues, if later); precondition: registered-mail notice of intent to foreclose with deficiency warning at least 21 days before the power-of-sale sale, plus affidavit of mailing within 30 days after the sale
deficiency.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 244, §§ 17A (2-year limitation), 17B (pre-sale deficiency notice and affidavit)

MA.notes: Massachusetts 12% prejudgment interest on contract claims is mandatory and simple, running from breach/demand. Fees: American rule; the lease fee-reciprocity statute (c. 186, s. 20) is limited to residential leases, so no reciprocity for commercial contracts; no general contract fee statute. Deficiency: no statutory FMV credit, but case law requires the foreclosing mortgagee to act in good faith and use reasonable diligence to obtain a fair price (not fetched).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date the liquidated sum was due (case law: prejudgment interest is a matter of right where the obligation to pay and the amount due became certain, definite and liquidated by a specific date)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Md. Const. art. III, § 57 (legal rate 6% unless otherwise provided by the General Assembly); Md. Code, Com. Law § 12-102 (6% simple default ceiling on loans except as otherwise provided by law)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 10% per annum on the amount of the judgment (6% for residential rent judgments, not relevant to commercial); for judgments on a contract for the loan of money NOT secured by a mortgage or deed of trust, the contract rate applies on unpaid principal until the originally scheduled maturity.

deficiency.timeLimit: Motion for deficiency judgment within 3 years after final ratification of the auditor's report
deficiency.citation: Md. Rule 14-216(b); Pulliam v. Dyck-O'Neal, Inc., No. 1080, Sept. Term 2018 (Md. Ct. Spec. App. 2019)

MD.notes: Maryland prejudgment interest: 6% legal rate; as of right for liquidated contract sums, discretionary otherwise (case law, not statute text). Postjudgment 10% fixed. Fees: American rule; no reciprocal or general contract fee statute located for commercial contracts. Deficiency: available after foreclosure sale via Rule 14-216(b) motion; no statutory FMV credit (computed from sale proceeds). The 3-year rule text was confirmed through court opinion and secondary sources, not the rule text itself.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: If the contract/note contains an interest provision: the contract rate (fixed as of notice of claim or complaint filing). Otherwise: weekly average 1-year constant-maturity Treasury yield for the last full week of the calendar year before the year interest begins to accrue + 3%. Rate must be stated in the judgment.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From service of a sworn notice of claim (personal service or registered/certified mail); if none, from the date the complaint is filed -- NOT from breach. Suspended during continuances >30 days obtained by the prevailing party; court may waive for good cause.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 1-year constant-maturity Treasury yield (last full week of the prior calendar year) + 6%; for a contract/note with an interest provision, the GREATER of the contract rate or that formula rate, fixed as of the judgment date. Accrues from entry, including during appeal; prejudgment interest is not added to the base.

deficiency.timeLimit: Report of sale must be filed within the earlier of 90 days after the public sale or 45 days after delivery of the deed (extendable for good cause on a timely motion); failure to file timely forfeits the deficiency
deficiency.citation: 14 M.R.S. § 6324 (deficiency assessed against the mortgagor; if the mortgagee buys at the sale, deficiency limited to sum due minus fair market value per independent appraisal)

ME.notes: Maine prejudgment interest runs from notice of claim/complaint, not from the breach date, which materially reduces the award for older arrears. The 1-year Treasury values for the relevant years were not verified here, so rates are formula-only (null). Fees: no reciprocity or general contract fee statute located; contract clauses enforced as written. Deficiency: judicial foreclosure by sale; FMV cap applies only when the foreclosing mortgagee is the buyer.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Statutory judgment interest runs from complaint filing (covers the prejudgment period). Written instrument evidencing indebtedness with a specified rate (complaints filed on/after July 1, 2002): the instrument rate (variable rates fixed at the rate in effect when the complaint is filed), capped at 13% compounded annually. Otherwise: 1% + average auction yield of 5-year Treasury notes for the prior 6 months, certified by the State Treasurer each Jan. 1 and July 1, reset at 6-month intervals, compounded annually, on the whole judgment including fees and costs. Certified 5-yr averages: 1/1/2025 4.016, 7/1/2025 4.083, 1/1/2026 3.725, 7/1/2026 3.959 (add 1%: current rate 4.959%).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date the complaint is filed (MCL 600.6013), not breach; pre-filing contract interest is recoverable only as contract damages (e.g., a lease/note rate)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same continuous computation under 600.6013 from filing to satisfaction: instrument rate (cap 13% compounded annually) or 1% + 5-yr Treasury auction average, reset every 6 months, compounded annually. 4.959% for the period beginning July 1, 2026.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: MCL § 600.6013(7)-(8); Michigan Dept. of Treasury, Interest Rates for Money Judgments

deficiency.citation: MCL § 600.3280 (after foreclosure by advertisement where the mortgagee/holder bought, the defendant in a deficiency suit may show the property was fairly worth the debt or the bid was substantially less than true value, defeating the deficiency in whole or in part)

MI.notes: Michigan has no stand-alone prejudgment interest statute for contract claims beyond 600.6013's from-filing interest; interest from breach to filing must come from the contract itself or as common-law damages. Fees: American rule; no reciprocity or general contract fee statute located. Deficiency: FMV operates as a defense/set-off when the lender bought at an advertisement sale. No deficiency-specific filing deadline located (timeLimit null).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Judgments/awards over $50,000 (non-government, non-family): 10% simple per year. $50,000 or less: rate set each December by the state court administrator from the 1-year constant-maturity Treasury yield, rounded to nearest 1%, floor 4%. Applies 'except as otherwise provided by contract or allowed by law'; settlement-offer comparison can cut off or reduce interest.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Earliest of commencement of the action, demand for arbitration, or a written notice of claim (suit must follow notice within 2 years) -- not the breach date under the statute
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Minn. Stat. § 549.09, subd. 1(b), (c)(1)-(2); § 334.01, subd. 1 (6% legal rate absent a written contract rate; contracts bear the same rate after maturity)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same 549.09 schedule until paid: over $50,000 = 10% per year; $50,000 or less = annual administrator rate (1-yr Treasury rounded, floor 4%), simple.

deficiency.citation: Minn. Stat. § 582.30, subds. 1-2 (deficiency allowed for the difference between the debt/judgment and net sale proceeds; barred after foreclosure by advertisement with a 6-month or 5-week redemption period; FMV determination and 90-day action required only for agricultural property)

MN.notes: Minnesota courts also recognize common-law prejudgment interest on liquidated contract damages from the date of breach, which a claimant may seek instead of 549.09 interest (case law, not verified here); where the lease/note fixes a rate, the contract rate governs. Rate field shows the 10% rate that applies to commercial claims over $50,000. Fees: no reciprocity (504B.172 is residential) or general contract fee statute located. Deficiency: for non-agricultural commercial property, deficiency is measured from sale proceeds with no FMV credit; whether it is barred depends on the redemption period that applied to the advertisement foreclosure (580.23, not fetched).
resolutions: 10% applies to judgments over $50,000 (Minn. Stat. 549.09); smaller judgments use the index rate

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Written contracts: when the money becomes due and payable; accounts: after due and demand of payment is made
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 408.020 (9% when no other rate is agreed)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Nontort actions: 9% per annum on the judgment balance (principal + prejudgment interest + costs/fees) from entry until satisfied; judgments upon contracts bearing MORE than 9% bear the contract rate. (Tort judgments: intended Federal Funds rate + 5%.)

feeShifting.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 408.092 (fees permitted to enforce a credit agreement if in the written agreement or, for credit from a for-profit business or credit union, up to 15% of the defaulted balance) -- creditor-side only

deficiency.citation: No anti-deficiency statute; deficiency = debt minus foreclosure sale price, not FMV (First Bank v. Fischer & Frichtel, Inc., 364 S.W.3d 216 (Mo. 2012), per Husch Blackwell summary); sale may be set aside only if the price is so inadequate it shocks the conscience

MO.notes: Missouri prejudgment interest on liquidated contract claims is available as of right under 408.020 at 9% or the agreed rate; tort prejudgment interest rules in 408.040(3) do not apply. Fees: American rule; no reciprocity or general contract fee statute. Deficiency: measured by sale price, no FMV credit; case citation comes from a law-firm summary rather than the opinion itself. No deficiency-specific deadline (note/guaranty limitations period governs).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: No prejudgment-interest statute for contract claims; courts award it in their discretion on liquidated claims (or where the denial of payment was frivolous/in bad faith), typically at the contract rate or the 8% legal rate of 75-17-1(1)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Discretionary; generally from the date the liquidated sum was due or demanded (case law)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 75-17-1(1) (legal rate 8% on notes, accounts and contracts absent a written contract rate); award governed by case law

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgments founded on a sale or contract bear the contract's rate; all other judgments bear a per annum rate set by the trial judge, from a date the judge finds fair but not before the complaint was filed.

feeShifting.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 11-53-81 (open accounts only: creditor recovers reasonable fees if debtor fails to pay within 30 days after itemized written demand; a debtor who prevails also recovers fees) -- reciprocal but limited to open-account suits, not leases or loans generally

deficiency.timeLimit: Suit on an installment note (or series of 3+ notes) secured by the foreclosed property must be brought within 1 year of the foreclosure sale
deficiency.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-23 (1-year limitation after foreclosure); FMV requirement is case law (lender-bidder must show the sale price reflected fair market value; bids well below FMV defeat or reduce the deficiency)

MS.notes: Prejudgment rate shown (8%) is the legal rate courts commonly use; the award itself is discretionary. Postjudgment rate for contract judgments is the contract rate; for a contract with no stated rate the statute is ambiguous and courts have applied a judge-set rate (rate null). Deficiency FMV rule is Mississippi Supreme Court case law summarized by secondary sources (Nolo; courts.ms.gov opinion), not statute; the 1-year bar in 15-1-23 applies to installment notes and is the statute-verified deadline.
resolutions: no statute; the court awards prejudgment interest at its discretion (8% cited in the reading)

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: The day the right to recover damages certain (or capable of being made certain by calculation) vested -- i.e., when payment was due (27-1-211); 10% runs after money becomes due on an instrument of writing or account stated (31-1-106)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Mont. Code Ann. §§ 27-1-211 (right to interest on liquidated damages from the day vested), 31-1-106(1) (10% a year unless an express written contract fixes a different rate; 365-day year)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Bank prime loan rate (Fed H.15) + 3%, with the prime rate set as of January 1 of each year and applied to judgments entered that calendar year; not compounded. A judgment on a contractual obligation specifying an interest rate bears the contract rate.

feeShifting.citation: Mont. Code Ann. § 28-3-704(1) (if a contract made after July 1, 1971 gives one party an express right to fees, all parties have the same right and the prevailing party recovers reasonable fees; exception only for condemnors under (2))

deficiency.allowed: judicial foreclosure only (for trust indentures foreclosed by advertisement, none)
deficiency.citation: Mont. Code Ann. §§ 71-1-317 (no deficiency against grantor, surety or guarantor after a trust indenture is foreclosed by advertisement and sale), 71-1-304 (trust indentures limited to parcels not exceeding 40 acres; beneficiary may elect judicial foreclosure), 71-1-222(1)-(2) (one-action rule; judicial foreclosure balance docketed as personal judgment), 71-1-232 (no deficiency on seller purchase-money mortgages)

MT.notes: Montana's Small Tract Financing Act (trust indentures, 40 acres or less) bars all deficiencies, including against guarantors, after nonjudicial sale; a lender must foreclose judicially (as a mortgage) to preserve a deficiency. 71-1-222(4)(m) lets a lender sue a guarantor whose guaranty is not secured by the same mortgage outside the one-action rule. No statutory FMV credit located for judicial foreclosure. Postjudgment rate depends on the Jan. 1 prime rate for the year of entry (not verified for 2026, so rate null).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Contract rate if the contract specifies one; otherwise the legal rate of 8% per annum (G.S. 24-1). Amount awarded on a contract bears interest from the date of breach (G.S. 24-5(a)); per UNC School of Government guidance, where damages are ascertainable from the contract, interest from breach is a matter of law.
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (statute sets a per-annum rate; no compounding provided)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date of breach (G.S. 24-5(a)). Fact finder must separate principal from interest in the award.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. 24-5(a); 24-1

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Principal bears interest until satisfied at the legal rate (8%, G.S. 24-1), unless the contract expressly provides that the contract rate applies after judgment, in which case the contract rate. Consumer/agricultural credit: lower of legal or contract rate. Pre-judgment interest does not itself bear post-judgment interest (only principal).

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: G.S. 6-21.6 validates (does not create) reciprocal attorneys'-fee provisions in business contracts: enforceable only if the provision binds all parties reciprocally and all parties sign the contract (by hand or qualifying e-signature); court may award reasonable fees per the contract, considering listed factors; fees capped at the amount in controversy in suits primarily for money damages (6-21.6(f)); percentage presumptions do not apply (6-21.6(d)). It does NOT convert a one-sided clause into a reciprocal one.
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: G.S. 6-21.2: fee obligations in a note, conditional sale contract or other evidence of indebtedness are enforceable when collected through an attorney after maturity, capped at 15% of the 'outstanding balance' (principal + interest owing when suit is filed); a clause for 'reasonable' fees without a percentage is construed as 15%; holder must give written notice after maturity that the debtor has 5 days from mailing to pay the outstanding balance without fees, and payment within that time voids the fee obligation. A party may elect 6-21.2 or 6-21.6 where both apply, but recover only once (6-21.6(e)).

deficiency.fmvLimit: Where the secured creditor itself buys at a power-of-sale (non-judicial) sale, the debtor may defend/offset a deficiency suit by showing the property was fairly worth the debt at the time and place of sale or that the bid was substantially less than true value (G.S. 45-21.36; not applicable to court-ordered foreclosure sales). Deficiency barred entirely on seller-financed purchase-money mortgages/deeds of trust showing on their face that they secure purchase money (G.S. 45-21.38).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action for a deficiency judgment after foreclosure must be brought within one year, running from delivery of the foreclosure deed (or earlier if the debt's own limitation period would expire sooner) (G.S. 1-54(6)).

NC.notes: Contract-rate-controls for prejudgment interest is from the UNC School of Government magistrate handout on G.S. 24-5 (https://www.sog.unc.edu/sites/default/files/course_materials/Lewandowski-Update%20Handout-Interest%20on%20Judgments_0.pdf), consistent with the statute's structure; not from statutory text itself. Whether G.S. 6-21.2 reaches commercial leases as an 'evidence of indebtedness' (NC case law has so held, e.g. Stillwell Enterprises) was not verified this session. G.S. 45-21.36 is an offset defense, not a mechanical FMV credit, and applies only when the creditor/holder is the purchaser at a non-judicial sale. G.S. 6-21.6 amended by S.L. 2025-25; text read from current ncleg.gov version.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date of breach (G.S. 24-5(a)); for missed rent/installments, each installment from its own breach date.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. 24-5(a); 24-1; Thomas M. McInnis & Assocs. v. Hall, 318 N.C. 421 (1986)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Legal rate of 8% (G.S. 24-1) on the principal until satisfied, unless the parties agreed in the contract that the contract rate shall apply after judgment, in which case the contract rate applies after entry of judgment (G.S. 24-5(a)). Consumer/agricultural credit contracts: lower of legal or contract rate.

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: G.S. 6-21.6: reciprocal attorneys' fee provisions in a business contract (each party agrees to pay the other's fees on terms applicable to all parties) are valid and enforceable for reasonable fees only if all parties sign the contract (by hand or qualifying electronic signature); the court or arbitrator 'may' award reasonable fees considering 13 listed factors; stated-percentage presumptions do not govern; in an action primarily for money damages, fees may not exceed the amount in controversy. It does NOT convert a one-sided clause into a reciprocal one.
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: G.S. 6-21.2: a fee obligation in a note, conditional sale contract or other 'evidence of indebtedness' (includes leases -- Stillwell Enters. v. Interstate Equip. Co., 300 N.C. 286 (1980)) is enforceable if collected through an attorney after maturity, capped at 15% of the 'outstanding balance'; a 'reasonable attorneys' fees' clause with no percentage is construed as 15% of the outstanding balance; the creditor must give written notice after maturity that the fee provision will be enforced, and the fee obligation is void if the debtor pays the outstanding balance within 5 days of mailing. Where a business contract is also an evidence of indebtedness, the party may elect 6-21.2 or 6-21.6 but recover only once (6-21.6(e)).

deficiency.allowed: Allowed after both power-of-sale and judicial foreclosure, except barred for a purchase-money mortgage/deed of trust securing the balance of the purchase price to the seller where the note shows on its face it is for purchase money (G.S. 45-21.38).
deficiency.fmvLimit: Power-of-sale sales where the lender (holder) buys at the sale: the debtor may show as a defense and offset (not a counterclaim) that the property was fairly worth the debt at the time and place of sale, or that the bid was substantially less than true value, to defeat or reduce the deficiency (G.S. 45-21.36). Does not apply to court-ordered (judicial) foreclosure sales or to third-party purchasers.
deficiency.timeLimit: One year from delivery of the foreclosure deed, or earlier if the underlying debt's own limitation period would expire sooner (G.S. 1-54(6)).

secondReading.notes: All statute text read on ncleg.gov. PREJUDGMENT: G.S. 24-5(a) says the contract award 'bears interest from the date of breach' but does not itself state the pre-judgment rate; the rule that the contract rate applies before judgment if the contract has one, otherwise the 8% legal rate (G.S. 24-1), and that where damages are ascertainable from the contract interest from breach is recoverable 'as a matter of law' (McInnis v. Hall, 318 N.C. 421, 431 (1986)), comes from the UNC School of Government handout 'Rules for Determining Interest on Judgments' (DGL/SOG, Oct. 2012), which also shows simple interest (Principal x Rate x Time). McInnis was verified only as quoted in that handout. POSTJUDGMENT: legal rate 8% unless the contract expressly provides the contract rate applies after judgment. POINTER CORRECTION: 6-21.6 is not a statute that makes one-sided clauses reciprocal -- it validates clauses that are already reciprocal, and only if all parties signed. NC's baseline (no fees absent statute) means a one-sided lease/note fee clause is enforceable only through 6-21.2's 15% cap and 5-day notice procedure. Stillwell (lease is an 'evidence of indebtedness') verified via search-result summaries of the NC Supreme Court opinion, medium confidence. No general contract fee statute beyond 6-21.2. DEFICIENCY: 45-21.38 bars deficiency only for seller-financed purchase money; third-party lender acquisition loans are not covered by its text.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Legal rate 6% per annum on any legal indebtedness unless a different rate (not above the usury cap in 47-14-09) is contracted for in writing (N.D.C.C. 47-14-05). A contract's stipulated rate remains chargeable after breach until superseded by verdict (47-14-07); contracts bear the same rate after maturity as before unless agreed otherwise in writing (47-14-05).
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (no compounding provided for prejudgment interest; 47-14-06 deems an unspecified-period rate an annual rate)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Damages certain or capable of being made certain by calculation carry interest from the day the right to recover them vested, except while the debtor is prevented by law or by the creditor's act from paying (N.D.C.C. 32-03-04). For non-contract obligations and cases of oppression, fraud or malice, interest is discretionary (32-03-05).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Rate in the original instrument on which the action is based (not above the 47-14-09 maximum); if none or not instrument-based, prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal on the first Monday in December plus 3 percentage points, rounded UP to the next 0.5%, set by the state court administrator by Dec 20 and effective Jan 1-Dec 31 of the following year; may not be compounded. Rate for judgments entered in 2026: 10.00% (prime 7.00% on Dec 1, 2025).

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: None. Instead N.D.C.C. 28-26-04 makes VOID as against public policy any attorney's-fee provision in a note, bond, mortgage, security agreement, or other evidence of debt for fees on default, collection, or foreclosure. A commercial lease is NOT an 'evidence of debt', so a lease fee clause is enforceable (T.F. James Co. v. Vakoch, 2001 ND 112).
feeShifting.citation: N.D.C.C. 28-26-04 (any provision in a note, bond, mortgage, security agreement or other evidence of debt for payment of an attorney's fee on default, collection, or foreclosure is against public policy and void)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Commercial real property (N.D.C.C. 32-19-06.1): court appoints an appraiser at plaintiff's request; court finds fair market value and prior liens at entry of the foreclosure judgment; after the sheriff's sale the clerk credits the bid less sale costs, but the credit may not be less than the court-found fair market value; deficiency = amount due under the foreclosure judgment with interest at the note rate, less that credit (see also 32-19-03: deficiency limited to difference between appraised value and amount due). Barred for owner-occupied homestead residential property of 4 or fewer units (32-19-03).
deficiency.timeLimit: No separate post-sale deadline for commercial property: the deficiency must be pleaded and demanded in the foreclosure action itself (32-19-04, 32-19-06.1), and the clerk enters the money judgment after the order confirming the sheriff's sale. (Agricultural land >40 acres uses a separate action within 90 days after the sheriff's sale, 32-19-06.2.)

ND.notes: N.D.C.C. 28-26-04 voids contractual attorney-fee clauses in notes, mortgages and other evidence of debt, so no fee award should be added for a commercial loan claim in ND. Whether 28-26-04 also voids a fee clause in a commercial LEASE (not listed expressly in the statute) was not verified; treat as unresolved. No reciprocal-fee or general contract-fee statute found. Postjudgment: if the note/lease carries its own rate, that rate (capped by 47-14-09) applies instead of the 10% default. Statute text read from the official ndlegis.gov Century Code chapter PDFs.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the day the right to recover damages that are certain or capable of being made certain by calculation vested (e.g., each rent/loan payment's due date), except while the debtor is prevented by law or by the creditor's act from paying (N.D.C.C. 32-03-04).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: If the judgment is based on an instrument with an interest rate: that rate (not above the 47-14-09 maximum). Otherwise: prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal on the first Monday in December plus 3 percentage points, rounded up to the next one-half point, set by the State Court Administrator by December 20 for judgments entered the following calendar year; not compounded.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: None. Instead N.D.C.C. 28-26-04 makes VOID as against public policy any attorney's-fee provision in a note, bond, mortgage, security agreement, or other evidence of debt for fees on default, collection, or foreclosure. A commercial lease is NOT an 'evidence of debt', so a lease fee clause is enforceable (T.F. James Co. v. Vakoch, 2001 ND 112).
feeShifting.citation: N.D.C.C. 28-26-04; T.F. James Co. v. Vakoch, 2001 ND 112, 628 N.W.2d 298

deficiency.allowed: Allowed for commercial real property, only through the judicial foreclosure action (foreclosure by advertisement/power of sale is limited to mortgages held by the state; all others must be foreclosed by action, 35-22-01). Barred for owner-occupied homestead residential property of 4 or fewer units on up to 40 acres; limited for agricultural land over 40 acres.
deficiency.fmvLimit: Commercial: the court finds fair market value (court-appointed licensed appraiser, plus affidavits/other proof) in the foreclosure judgment; on confirmation the clerk credits the sheriff's-sale bid less sale costs, but the credit may not be less than the court-established fair market value; deficiency = amount due in the foreclosure judgment plus interest at the note rate, less that credit (32-19-06.1; 32-19-03).
deficiency.timeLimit: No separate post-sale deadline for commercial property: the deficiency must be demanded in the foreclosure pleading, naming the personally liable parties (32-19-06.1, 32-19-04), and the clerk enters it upon the order confirming the sheriff's sale. (The 90-day separate-action deadline and 3-year enforcement limit in 32-19-06.2 apply only to agricultural land over 40 acres.)

secondReading.notes: All statute text read from the official ndlegis.gov chapter PDFs. PREJUDGMENT: 32-03-04 gives a right ('is entitled to recover') to interest on damages certain or calculable from the day vested; discretionary interest under 32-03-05 applies only to obligations NOT arising from contract (and oppression/fraud/malice), so liquidated contract claims fall under 32-03-04. Rate: the legal rate is 6% per annum under 47-14-05 unless a different rate (not above the 47-14-09 maximum) is contracted for in writing, and contracts bear the same rate after maturity as before unless agreed otherwise in writing; compounding not specified in these sections (left null). The pairing of 32-03-04 with the 47-14-05 rate is inferred from the statute texts, not from a verified case. POSTJUDGMENT: 2026 rate is 10.00% for judgments entered Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026 (prime rate on Dec 1, 2025 was 7.00%), per the North Dakota Court System announcement dated Dec 1, 2025 (https://www.ndcourts.gov/news/north-dakota/north-dakota-supreme-court/general-news/interest-rate-set-for-2026-judgments). An instrument's own rate carries into the judgment. FEES: no reciprocal-fee statute found; 28-26-04 voids fee clauses in loan documents (notes, mortgages, guaranty-type evidence of debt) -- so a commercial lender's contractual fee clause is unenforceable, but a commercial landlord's is enforceable per T.F. James Co. v. Vakoch (holding verified via FindLaw's copy of the opinion). POINTER CORRECTIONS: 32-19-07 is not an FMV provision (it allows suit on the note for junior residential mortgages if foreclosure is waived); the FMV rules are in 32-19-03 and 32-19-06.1; 32-19-04 governs complaint contents. 28-20-34's formula verified as pointed (prime + 3, rounded up to next 1/2 point).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 12% per annum on money due on any instrument in writing, unless otherwise agreed (Neb. Rev. Stat. 45-104); applied to liquidated claims by 45-103.02(2).
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (statute states a per-annum rate and does not provide for compounding)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Liquidated claims: from the date the cause of action arose until entry of judgment (45-103.02(2)). Unliquidated claims: judgment rate under 45-103 only from the date of a qualifying written settlement offer that the judgment exceeds (45-103.02(1)).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgments on/after July 20, 2002: 2 percentage points above the bond investment yield (published by the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury) of the average accepted auction price for the first auction of each annual quarter of 26-week U.S. Treasury bills in effect on the date of entry of judgment. Fixed at entry. Does not apply where the parties' written or oral contract agreed a different rate, or where another statute sets the rate.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-1801: on claims of $4,000 or less unpaid 90 days after accrual, the plaintiff may recover a fee of $10 plus 10% of the judgment in excess of $50 (subject to the statute's demand/notice conditions). Otherwise fees only where a statute or uniform course of procedure allows; contractual fee clauses are against public policy and not enforced (Stewart v. Bennett (Neb. 2007); Parkert v. Lindquist).
feeShifting.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-1801; Stewart v. Bennett (Neb. 2007)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency limited to the amount by which the debt plus interest and sale costs/trustee fees exceeds the fair market value of the property as of the sale date, and in no event more than the debt minus the sale price (i.e., credit is the greater of FMV or sale price).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action must be commenced within three months after the trustee's sale.
deficiency.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1013 (Nebraska Trust Deeds Act)

NE.notes: Nebraska refuses to enforce contractual attorney-fee clauses, so a commercial lease/note fee clause yields no fee award unless a statute authorizes one; the calculator should not add contractual fees for NE. Postjudgment rate is a floating formula fixed at entry (no single number stored). Deficiency rule recorded is for trust-deed (power of sale) foreclosures, the usual commercial vehicle; judicial mortgage foreclosure deficiencies were not separately verified. Stewart v. Bennett holding verified on FindLaw (https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/ne-supreme-court/1083288.html); reporter cite not independently confirmed so omitted.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Liquidated claims: from the date the cause of action arose until entry of judgment (Neb. Rev. Stat. 45-103.02(2)). Unliquidated claims: only from the date of plaintiff's first certified-mail written offer of settlement that the judgment exceeds, if the offer conditions in 45-103.02(1) are met, at the 45-103 judgment rate.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 45-103.02(2) (liquidated claims accrue interest 'as provided in section 45-104'); Neb. Rev. Stat. 45-104 ('Unless otherwise agreed, interest shall be allowed at the rate of twelve percent per annum on money due on any instrument in writing ... and on money loaned or due and withheld by unreasonable delay of payment')

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 2 percentage points above the bond investment yield, as published by the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury, of the average accepted auction price for the first auction of each annual quarter of 26-week U.S. Treasury bills in effect on the date of entry of judgment (judgments on/after July 20, 2002). Accrues from entry of judgment until satisfaction (45-103.01). Does not apply where the parties to a contract agreed a different rate (45-103(2)) or where a rate is specifically provided by law.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-1801: only on lawsuits of $4,000 or less, where the claim is unpaid 90 days after it accrued; fee is $10 plus 10% of the judgment over $50 (with 6% interest from 30 days after accrual). Not relevant to typical commercial-lease or loan claims above $4,000.
feeShifting.citation: Hand Cut Steaks Acquisitions v. Lone Star Steakhouse, 298 Neb. 705, 905 N.W.2d 644 (2018) (syllabus pt. 40: 'In the absence of a uniform course of procedure or authorization by statute, contractual agreements for attorney fees are against public policy and will not be judicially enforced'; declining to depart from that rule); Stewart v. Bennett, 273 Neb. 17, 727 N.W.2d 424 (2007); Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-1801

deficiency.allowed: Trust deed (trustee's sale): allowed by action commenced within 3 months after the sale, capped at debt + interest + costs/expenses of sale (incl. trustee's fees) minus the court-found fair market value at the date of sale (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1013). Judicial mortgage foreclosure: deficiency allowed as a continuation of the foreclosure suit; while foreclosure is pending and after decree, no separate action at law on the secured debt without court authorization (Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-2140).
deficiency.fmvLimit: Trust deed: judgment cannot exceed debt + interest + costs of sale minus fair market value at date of sale (76-1013). Judicial mortgage foreclosure of non-agricultural property: no statutory FMV limit verified.
deficiency.timeLimit: Trust deed: action within 3 months after the trustee's sale (76-1013). Judicial foreclosure: no separate statutory deadline verified (sought within the foreclosure case).
deficiency.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1013; Neb. Rev. Stat. 25-2140

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment: 12% under 45-104 applies 'unless otherwise agreed', so a lease/note rate displaces it. 'Liquidated' is a case-law concept (no reasonable controversy over the right to recover or the amount) not defined in the statute. The statute does not provide for compounding; 'simple' reflects the per-annum rate as written. Post-judgment: the Nebraska Judicial Branch publishes the 45-103 rate; current published rate is 5.970% effective July 16, 2026 (nebraskajudicial.gov/rules/administrative-policies-schedules/judgment-interest-rate). postjudgmentInterest.rate left null because it is a formula that changes quarterly. Fees: Nebraska refuses to enforce contractual attorney-fee clauses in judicial proceedings absent a statute or uniform course of procedure (public-policy rule reaffirmed in a commercial case in 2018); no reciprocal-fee statute found. Pointer correction: 45-103 is the formula statute and uses the first auction of each annual quarter (not a rate re-set at each judgment); 45-103.02 is prejudgment accrual; 45-104 applies 'unless otherwise agreed'. Deficiency: Nebraska's statutory FMV limit for judicial foreclosure applies to agricultural land only per secondary sources (not verified from statute text, and not relevant to commercial non-ag property).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Annual simple rate set by the State Treasurer: prevailing discount rate on 26-week U.S. Treasury bills at the last auction before the last day of September, plus 2 percentage points, rounded to nearest 0.1%; transmitted by Dec 1 and in effect Jan 1-Dec 31 of the following year (RSA 336:1, II). Published rates: 2026 5.7%, 2025 6.2%, 2024 7.3%, 2023 5.8%, 2022 2.0% (NH Judicial Branch). 'rate' field = 2026 rate.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Action on a debt, account stated, or for liquidated damages: from pre-suit demand if one was made; absent a pre-suit demand, from the institution of suit (RSA 524:1-a). Other civil damages: from the date of the writ or filing of the petition to judgment, added by the clerk (RSA 524:1-b).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same RSA 336:1, II annual simple rate (26-week T-bill discount rate at last auction before Sept 30 + 2 points, rounded to 0.1%), reset each Jan 1. 2026 = 5.7%.
postjudgmentInterest.citation: RSA 336:1, II; rate table at NH Judicial Branch Civil Interest Rates page

feeShifting.citation: RSA 361-C:1-2 (consumer only, not applicable to commercial contracts)

deficiency.citation: No deficiency statute in RSA ch. 479; RSA 508:6 (actions on mortgage notes may be brought so long as an action on the mortgage may be); Murphy v. Financial Development Corp., 126 N.H. 536 (1985) (mortgagee's duty of good faith and due diligence to obtain a fair price at power-of-sale foreclosure)

NH.notes: RSA 361-C:2 makes a lender/seller fee clause reciprocal but only for consumer credit/retail installment contracts (proceeds used primarily for personal, household or family purposes, RSA 361-C:1), so it does not reach commercial leases or loans; no commercial reciprocal or general contract fee statute found. contractRateControls left null: RSA 336:1, I sets a 10% default rate for business transactions 'unless otherwise agreed upon in writing' and permits agreed compound interest, but RSA 336:1, II separately fixes the rate for prejudgment interest on judgments; I did not find a statute or verified case saying which governs pre-judgment accrual on a note/lease with its own rate. RSA 524:1-a text says interest runs from institution of suit only 'in the absence of a demand prior to' suit; the demand-date start is the statute's implication, not an express sentence. Deficiency: New Hampshire has no statutory fair-market-value cap or deficiency deadline found; the Murphy good-faith/due-diligence duty (sale price must be fair and reasonable) is case law, verified via search-result summaries of the opinion (medium confidence), so fmvLimit and timeLimit are null.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Annual simple rate set by the state treasurer: prevailing discount rate on 26-week U.S. Treasury bills at the last auction preceding the last day of September, plus 2 percentage points, rounded to the nearest tenth; determined by December 1 and effective January 1-December 31 of the following year. Applies to judgments 'including prejudgment interest'.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Clerk adds interest on damages from the date of the writ or filing of the petition to the date of judgment (RSA 524:1-b, mandatory). For an action on a debt/account stated or liquidated damages, absent a pre-suit demand interest runs from institution of suit (RSA 524:1-a), implying it may run from an earlier demand.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: RSA 336:1, II (judgment and prejudgment rate); RSA 524:1-a; RSA 524:1-b

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same RSA 336:1, II annual simple rate (26-week T-bill discount rate at last auction before Sept 30, + 2 points, rounded to nearest tenth), effective Jan 1-Dec 31 of the following year.

feeShifting.citation: RSA 361-C:1, 361-C:2 (reciprocal fees limited to consumer retail installment contracts and consumer loans; not applicable to commercial contracts)

deficiency.citation: No deficiency statute found in RSA ch. 479 (power-of-sale foreclosure). Mortgagee's duty of good faith and due diligence to obtain a fair price at a power-of-sale foreclosure: Murphy v. Financial Development Corp., 126 N.H. 536, 495 A.2d 1245 (1985).

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment: RSA 336:1, I separately sets a 10% annual rate 'in all business transactions in which interest is paid or secured, unless otherwise agreed upon in writing' (consumer credit excluded), while RSA 336:1, II sets the judgment rate 'including prejudgment interest'. Whether a lease/note contract rate displaces the 336:1, II rate for prejudgment or post-judgment interest is not answered by the statute text and was not verified from case law, so contractRateControls is null.
