Current rate: official NH Judicial Branch and State Treasury pages (courts.nh.gov civil-interest-rates; treasury.nh.gov interest-rates-judgments) both returned 403 to direct fetch; search-indexed text of those pages gives 2026 = 5.7% (Jan 1-Dec 31, 2026), 2025 = 6.2%, 2024 = 7.3%. Treat 5.7% as medium confidence until read directly. Fees: RSA 361-C (the pointer) is consumer-only; no general or reciprocal commercial fee statute found; one-sided contractual fee clauses are enforced as written under general contract law (not separately verified). Deficiency: NH forecloses mainly by power of sale (RSA 479:25); no statute located that bars, caps (FMV), or time-limits a commercial deficiency action, so fmvLimit and timeLimit are null. Deficiency is pursued by suit on the note; Murphy imposes a good-faith/due-diligence duty to get a fair price (breach is measured against a fair price, per secondary summaries), which is a defense/offset, not a statutory FMV cap. Limitations period for the note suit not verified. Pointer corrections: the RSA 336 URL is under Title XXXI, not XXXIII; RSA 479:27 not found to address deficiencies.

resolutions: 2026 rate 5.7% from court and Treasury pages read via search index; medium confidence

prejudgmentInterest.formula: No statutory rate for contract claims. Award and rate both lie in the trial court's equitable discretion (Litton Industries, Inc. v. IMO Industries, Inc., N.J. Nov. 2, 2009). R. 4:42-11(b) (fixed prejudgment interest formula) applies only to tort actions. Courts commonly look to the R. 4:42-11(a) judgment rates as a benchmark, but that is practice, not a rule for contract cases.
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: discretionary (not fixed by rule for contract claims)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: discretionary
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Litton Industries, Inc. v. IMO Industries, Inc. (N.J. 2009); R. 4:42-11(b) (tort only)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Simple interest. R. 4:42-11(a)(ii): average rate of return, to nearest whole or half percent, of the State of New Jersey Cash Management Fund (State accounts) for the fiscal year ending the preceding June 30, floor 0.25%, set per calendar year. R. 4:42-11(a)(iii): for judgments exceeding the Special Civil Part monetary limit at entry, that rate plus 2% per annum. Calendar 2026: 4.5% (at/below Special Civil Part limit), 6.5% (above). 'rate' field = 2026 rate for judgments above the Special Civil Part limit, which covers most commercial lease/loan judgments.

feeShifting.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.66 (reciprocal fee covenant applies to residential leases only; not commercial)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Obligor may answer disputing the deficiency; both sides may offer evidence of the premises' fair market value at the time of the foreclosure sale, and the court determines the deficiency by deducting that fair market value from the secured debt (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-3).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action on the bond/note for the deficiency must be commenced within 3 months from the date of the sale, or from confirmation of the sale if confirmation is required; foreclosure must come first, and no action lies against an obligor not joined in the foreclosure (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-2).

NJ.notes: Prejudgment interest on a commercial contract claim in New Jersey is discretionary in both award and rate, so the calculator cannot compute a fixed figure; contractRateControls left null because no rule or statute on that point was verified (courts frequently award the contract rate, but that is not verified here). The Special Civil Part monetary limit ($20,000 per secondary sources) was not verified against the rule text; the postjudgment rate chosen for a given judgment depends on it. Rule 4:42-11 text read from courtrules.net mirror; the 2026 rates are from the NJ Courts notice. No New Jersey statute making a one-sided commercial fee clause reciprocal was found; the American Rule applies and contractual fee clauses are enforced per their terms (case law, not verified here).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Set by the trial court on equitable principles (no statute or rule fixes the start date for contract claims). R. 4:42-11(b)'s start date (later of filing or 6 months after accrual) applies to tort actions only.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: County of Essex v. First Union Nat'l Bank, 186 N.J. 46, 61 (2006) (award and calculation of prejudgment interest in a contract action is within the trial court's sound discretion); Litton Indus., Inc. v. IMO Indus., Inc., 200 N.J. 372, 390 (2009) ('the award of prejudgment interest on contract and equitable claims is based on equitable principles'); Van Note-Harvey Assocs., P.C. v. Twp. of East Hanover, 175 N.J. 535, 542 (2003) (where the claim for interest is based on the contract's own provisions, the party 'must be required to comply with its contractual obligations') -- as quoted and applied in Rutgers v. Ndukwe, No. A-3659-23 (N.J. App. Div. 2025) (reversing denial of note-rate interest)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Simple interest, 'except as otherwise ordered by the court or provided by law'. Judgments not exceeding the Special Civil Part monetary limit ($20,000) at entry: average rate of return, to the nearest whole or one-half percent, of the State of New Jersey Cash Management Fund (State accounts) for the preceding fiscal year ending June 30, as reported by the Division of Investment; reset each calendar year. Judgments exceeding that limit: the same rate plus 2% per annum (since Sept. 1, 1996).

feeShifting.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.66 (implied reciprocal fee covenant applies only to a 'residential lease agreement'; not applicable to commercial leases)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Obligor may answer disputing the deficiency; the court (with or without a jury) determines the deficiency by deducting from the secured debt the fair market value of the premises at the time of the foreclosure sale (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-3). Judgment limited to the balance due on the debt, interest and costs (2A:50-2).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action on the bond or note for the deficiency must be commenced within 3 months from the date of the sale, or from the date of confirmation of the sale if confirmation is required (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-2). Obligor must have been made a party to the foreclosure action.

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest on a contract claim is discretionary/equitable, so rate and compounding are null; trial courts commonly look to the R. 4:42-11 rate as a guide (Pressler & Verniero comment cited in Ndukwe) but that is not mandatory. A contractual interest rate in the note/lease is enforced for the pre-judgment period (Van Note-Harvey). Post-judgment: NJ Courts Notice to the Bar dated July 10, 2025 sets calendar-year 2026 (from Jan 1, 2026) rates at 4.5% for judgments not exceeding the Special Civil Part limit and 6.5% for judgments exceeding it; the limit is $20,000 per the 2022 amendment to R. 6:1-2 (from njcourts.gov search results, not read from the rule text). Whether a contract rate carries into the judgment is not addressed by the rule text beyond 'except as otherwise ordered by the court or provided by law' (not verified from case law). Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute for commercial contracts and no general contract-claim fee statute found; contractual fee clauses are enforced under case law (not separately verified here). Deficiency: New Jersey forecloses judicially only (no power of sale located); Fair Foreclosure Act is residential. Pointer corrections: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-6.1 is a 5-business-day rent grace-period statute, not a fee statute; the residential reciprocal-fee statute is 2A:18-61.66. Statute texts read from FindLaw (Justia returned a bot challenge, which was not bypassed).

resolutions: prejudgment interest on contract claims is discretionary (County of Essex v. First Union, 186 N.J. 46; Litton, 200 N.J. 372); a contractual interest rate must be enforced (Van Note-Harvey, 175 N.J. 535)

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Two tracks. (1) NMSA 56-8-3(A): on 'money due by contract', absent a written contract fixing a different rate, interest 'shall be not more than fifteen percent annually' (a ceiling, not a fixed rate); per the statute's annotations (Kueffer v. Kueffer, 1990-NMSC-045) this is recoverable as a matter of right when the amount due is ascertainable with reasonable certainty by a mathematical standard fixed in the contract or by established market prices. (2) NMSA 56-8-4(B): otherwise the court in its discretion may allow interest of up to 10% from the date the complaint is served, considering plaintiff delay and any reasonable pre-suit settlement offer by defendant.
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (statutes state an annual rate; no compounding provided)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: 56-8-3: from when the money is due under the contract (settled matured accounts: from the day the balance is ascertained). 56-8-4(B): from service of the complaint on the defendant.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 8.75% per year from entry, unless (1) the judgment is on a written instrument with a different rate, in which case interest is at a rate no higher than the instrument's rate, or (2) the judgment is based on tortious conduct, bad faith, or intentional or willful acts, in which case 15%.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: NMSA 39-2-2.1: in an action to recover on an open account, the prevailing party may be allowed a reasonable attorney fee set by the court. Limited to open accounts; does not reach commercial lease or note claims generally. (39-2-2 debtor fees applies only to UCC/retail-installment personal-property deficiencies.)

deficiency.timeLimit: Deed of Trust Act trustee's sale: separate deficiency action must be commenced within six years after the trustee's sale; if not, the sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction (NMSA 48-10-17(A)-(B)).

NM.notes: NM 56-8-3 sets a 15% ceiling, not a fixed rate, so 'rate' is null and 'rateCap' = 15; whether a trial court must award the full 15% on a liquidated contract claim was not verified from a primary source (the 'as a matter of right' rule comes from Justia's annotation summary of Kueffer). Deficiency: under 48-10-17(A) the deficiency is total owed (plus prior liens) minus the trustee's-sale price, with interest from sale at the contract rate; no fair-market-value offset in that statute, hence fmvLimit null. A deed of trust may itself prohibit deficiency recovery (48-10-17(D)); residential low-income bar (48-10-17(E)) is not relevant to commercial loans. Deficiencies after judicial mortgage foreclosure (the more common NM route) were not separately verified. No New Mexico statute making one-sided contractual fee clauses reciprocal was found in NMSA ch. 39, art. 2.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Ceiling of 15% per year: NMSA 56-8-3(A) sets interest on money due by contract at 'not more than fifteen percent annually' absent a written contract fixing a different rate; the court fixes the rate at or below 15%. Alternative: NMSA 56-8-4(B) discretionary interest of up to 10% from service of the complaint.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: 56-8-3: from when the money became due under the contract (case law; for settled matured accounts the statute says from the day the balance is ascertained). 56-8-4(B): from the date the complaint is served on the defendant.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: NMSA 1978, § 56-8-3; § 56-8-4(B); Sunwest Bank of Albuquerque v. Colucci, 1994-NMSC-027, 117 N.M. 373; Public Service Co. v. Diamond D Constr. Co., 2001-NMCA-082

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 8.75% per year from entry; if the judgment is on a written instrument with a different rate, interest at a rate no higher than the instrument's rate; 15% if the judgment is based on tortious conduct, bad faith, or intentional or willful acts.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: No general contract fee statute. NMSA 39-2-2.1 allows the prevailing party a reasonable attorney fee (discretionary, 'may be allowed') only in an action to recover on an open account. NMSA 47-8-48 (prevailing-party fees on rental agreements) is part of the Uniform Owner-Resident Relations Act (residential) and does not apply to commercial leases.

deficiency.allowed: Allowed. Trustee's (power-of-sale) sale under the Deed of Trust Act: only by a separate civil action commenced within six years after the sale; if none is commenced, the sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction. Judicial foreclosure: deficiency permitted; no statutory bar found for commercial loans. Barred only for a residential loan to a low-income household (<=80% AMI).
deficiency.timeLimit: Deed of trust (trustee's sale): separate action within 6 years after the trustee's sale. Judicial foreclosure: no specific statutory deadline found.

secondReading.notes: Statute text read on FindLaw (Justia and nmonesource returned 403/Cloudflare to the fetch tool). PREJUDGMENT: 56-8-3 is a ceiling ('not more than fifteen percent'), not a fixed rate, so rate is null; courts treat 56-8-3 interest on a contract sum ascertainable with reasonable certainty as a matter of right subject to countervailing equities (Sunwest Bank v. Colucci, 1994-NMSC-027 -- NMSC citation corrected from the pointer's absence of one; CourtListener snippet of Public Service Co. v. Diamond D, 2001-NMCA-082: 'Section 56-8-3 allows prejudgment interest as a matter of right'), and otherwise discretionary. Full opinion text could not be fetched (CourtListener/Justia blocked), so the 'matter of right' standard rests on CourtListener search snippets and Justia annotations (Kueffer v. Kueffer, 1990-NMSC-045; Grynberg v. Roberts, 102 N.M. 560 (1985), interest from dates payments were due) -- medium confidence. 56-8-4(B) (up to 10% from service of complaint, discretionary, weighing plaintiff delay and defendant's settlement offers) is a separate, alternative route and is not limited to torts. A written contract rate displaces the 15% ceiling (56-8-3 'in the absence of a written contract fixing a different rate'). POSTJUDGMENT: fixed 8.75% from entry; when the judgment is rendered on a written instrument having a different rate, interest is computed 'at a rate no higher than specified in the instrument' (the instrument rate is the ceiling for that judgment). FEES: no reciprocal-fee statute found after searching; enforceability of one-sided clauses left to contract. DEFICIENCY: no fair-value offset in 48-10-17 (deficiency = total owing less trustee's sale price). The pointer that the Deed of Trust Act is 'commercial only' could not be confirmed from 48-10-3's definitions, which exclude only farm and mineral real estate; not verified. Deficiency interest runs from the sale at the deed-of-trust/contract rate.

resolutions: rate is set by the court at or below 15% on money due by contract (NMSA 56-8-3)

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate at the largest bank in Nevada, as ascertained by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions on the January 1 or July 1 immediately preceding the date of the transaction, plus 2%; adjusted each January 1 and July 1 thereafter until the judgment is satisfied (NRS 99.040(1)). Where the claim is reduced to judgment without a contract/statutory/judgment rate, NRS 17.130(2) runs the same prime+2% formula from service of the summons and complaint.
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (statutes state an annual rate; no compounding provided)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time the money becomes due, on contracts express or implied and other listed obligations (NRS 99.040(1)); NRS 17.130(2) default (no other rate provided) runs from service of summons and complaint.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: When no rate is provided by contract or law or specified in the judgment: prime rate at the largest bank in Nevada as ascertained by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions on the January 1 or July 1 immediately preceding the judgment, plus 2%, adjusted each January 1 and July 1 until satisfied. A contract rate, if provided, applies instead.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: NRS 18.010(2)(a): court may award fees to a prevailing party who has not recovered more than $20,000; NRS 18.010(2)(b): fees regardless of amount where the opposing claim/defense was brought or maintained without reasonable ground or to harass. Otherwise fees follow the parties' agreement (NRS 18.010(1)).

deficiency.fmvLimit: Judgment may not exceed the lesser of (a) the debt minus the fair market value of the property at the time of sale, or (b) the debt minus the actual sale price, each with interest from the date of sale (NRS 40.459(2)). Additional limits apply only to owner-occupied 1-4 family residences and to assignees of the deficiency right on such property.
deficiency.timeLimit: Application must be made within 6 months after the foreclosure sale; if multiple parcels/liens secure the debt, 6 months after the sale of the last parcel, but no more than 2 years after the initial sale (NRS 40.455(1)-(2)).
deficiency.citation: NRS 40.455; NRS 40.459; one-action rule NRS 40.430

NV.notes: Prejudgment and postjudgment statutory rates are floating (prime at largest Nevada bank + 2%, reset semiannually); the calculator needs a lookup of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions' semiannual prime figure, not stored here. NRS 99.040 applies only where there is no express written contract fixing a different rate. Nevada has no statute making a one-sided contractual fee clause reciprocal (not found). NRS 40.459 text quoted from the 2026 NRS on leg.state.nv.us; note the subsection numbering there (the 'lesser of' limit is subsection 2, subsection 1 directs the money judgment).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate at the largest bank in Nevada, as ascertained by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions on January 1 or July 1 (whichever immediately precedes the date of the transaction), plus 2 percent; adjusted each January 1 and July 1 thereafter until the judgment is satisfied.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time the money becomes due (NRS 99.040(1)) on contracts, express or implied, other than book accounts. (NRS 17.130(2), the judgment-interest default, runs from service of summons and complaint where no contract/law rate applies.)
prejudgmentInterest.citation: NRS 99.040(1) ('When there is no express contract in writing fixing a different rate of interest, interest must be allowed at a rate equal to the prime rate at the largest bank in Nevada ... plus 2 percent, upon all money from the time it becomes due'); NRS 99.050 (parties may agree any rate and compounding)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: When no rate is provided by contract or otherwise by law, or specified in the judgment: prime rate at the largest bank in Nevada as ascertained by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions on the January 1 or July 1 immediately preceding the date of judgment, plus 2 percent, adjusted each January 1 and July 1 until satisfied. A contract rate carries into the judgment.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: NRS 18.010(2)(a): court may award fees to a prevailing party who has not recovered more than $20,000; 18.010(2)(b): fees where a claim/defense was maintained without reasonable ground or to harass. Per NRS 18.010(4), subsections 2 and 3 do not apply to an action arising out of a written instrument that entitles the prevailing party to reasonable attorney's fees (the contract clause governs instead). Contractual fee clauses are enforceable (NRS 18.010(1): compensation governed by agreement).

deficiency.fmvLimit: After a mandatory FMV hearing (NRS 40.457), the judgment may not exceed the lesser of (a) the secured indebtedness minus the fair market value of the property at the time of sale, or (b) the indebtedness minus the actual sale price, each with interest from the date of sale (NRS 40.459). An extra limit (for a judgment right acquired from a prior holder) applies to 1-4 family residential property only.
deficiency.timeLimit: Application within 6 months after the date of the foreclosure sale (NRS 40.455(1)); applies to both sheriff's (judicial) sale and trustee's sale.
deficiency.citation: NRS 40.430 (one-action rule); NRS 40.455(1); NRS 40.457(1); NRS 40.459

secondReading.notes: Current published rate: the Nevada Financial Institutions Division's prime-rate table (fid.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/fidnvgov/content/Resources/prime_interest_rate.pdf) shows prime of 6.75% for January 1, 2026 and 6.75% for July 1, 2026, so the NRS 99.040 / 17.130 rate is 8.75% for Jan 1-Dec 31, 2026 (Washoe County courts' legal-interest table also lists 8.75% for both 2026 halves). July 1, 2025 prime was 7.50% (9.50%). The FID table notes (AG Op. 98-20) that NRS 99.040 interest is simple. NRS 99.040 does not apply to obligations under NRS Chapter 624 (contractors). Fees: searched NRS Chapter 18 and secondary lists; no statute makes a one-sided fee clause reciprocal (no statute found). Deficiency: NRS 40.430 one-action rule requires the secured creditor to proceed against the collateral in one action; deficiency statutes apply to guarantors and sureties as well as the debtor (40.459(1)). The subsection numbering of 40.459 was read from nevada.public.law (the leg.state.nv.us Chapter 40 page truncated before these sections); verify numbering if citing to a subsection. Pointer corrections: none of substance; 18.010(2)(a) threshold is 'not recovered more than $20,000'.

resolutions: 2026 rate 8.75%: Nevada prime 6.75% (Commissioner of Financial Institutions, Jan 1 and Jul 1, 2026) + 2 (NRS 99.040)

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 9% per annum (CPLR 5004(a)), except 2% in an action on a consumer debt against a natural person (not relevant to commercial claims). Mandatory on a sum awarded for breach of contract (CPLR 5001(a)); discretionary only in actions of an equitable nature. Interest from verdict/decision to judgment is also added (CPLR 5002).
prejudgmentInterest.compounding: simple (Spodek v. Park Prop. Dev. Assocs., 96 N.Y.2d 577 (2001): CPLR 5001 provides simple interest, which runs on each missed installment of principal and contractual interest from its due date)
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the earliest ascertainable date the cause of action existed; damages incurred later bear interest from the date incurred, and items incurred at various times may be computed item by item or from a single reasonable intermediate date (CPLR 5001(b)). For installment rent/loan payments, each missed payment accrues from its own due date.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: CPLR 5001, 5002, 5004; NML Capital v. Republic of Argentina, 17 N.Y.3d 250 (2011); J. D'Addario & Co. v. Embassy Indus., 20 N.Y.3d 113 (2012)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Every money judgment bears interest from entry (CPLR 5003) at 9% per annum (CPLR 5004(a)); 2% only for consumer-debt judgments against natural persons.

feeShifting.citation: Real Property Law 234 (implied reciprocal fee covenant, residential leases only; no commercial counterpart found)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency = amount owed per the judgment with interest + prior liens with interest + costs, disbursements and referee's fees, less the HIGHER of the court-determined fair and reasonable market value (as of the auction date) or the sale price (RPAPL 1371(2)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Motion for leave to enter a deficiency judgment must be made with the motion to confirm the sale, within 90 days after the deed is delivered to the purchaser; if no timely motion, the sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction (RPAPL 1371(2)-(3)).
deficiency.citation: RPAPL 1371

NY.notes: Contract-rate rule: NML Capital (per the Court of Appeals slip opinion and secondary summaries) holds parties may fix by contract the rate that runs until judgment, with the 9% statutory rate as the default when the contract is silent on post-maturity/post-breach interest; D'Addario (read on nycourts.gov) holds contract terms can displace CPLR 5001 interest entirely where the contract makes a remedy exclusive. Whether a contract rate continues after judgment turns on contract language (not separately verified), so the calculator should default to 9% post-judgment. Fee shifting: NY follows the American Rule and enforces commercial fee clauses as written; RPL 234 reciprocity is expressly limited to 'leases of residential property' (verified on nysenate.gov), so reciprocalStatute is null for commercial leases/loans. The American Rule and enforcement of commercial fee clauses as written are general case law, not verified here.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the earliest ascertainable date the cause of action existed; damages incurred later run from the date incurred, and where damages were incurred at various times, interest runs on each item from its date or on all from a single reasonable intermediate date (CPLR 5001(b)). For installment obligations, from the date each payment became due (Spodek). Interest continues from verdict/decision to judgment (CPLR 5002).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: N.Y. CPLR 5001(a)-(b), 5004; Citibank, N.A. v. Liebowitz, 110 A.D.2d 615 (2d Dep't 1985); Spodek v. Park Prop. Dev. Assocs., 96 N.Y.2d 577 (2001)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: CPLR 5003: every money judgment bears interest from entry at the CPLR 5004 rate (9% per annum; 2% in an action arising out of a consumer debt where a natural person is a defendant -- not applicable to commercial claims). A contract rate governs only until the contract merges into the judgment; thereafter the statutory rate applies.

feeShifting.citation: N.Y. Real Prop. Law 234 (residential leases only); N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law 5-327 (consumer contracts only)

deficiency.allowed: Allowed in judicial foreclosure, by motion under RPAPL 1371; the plaintiff must also elect remedies -- while a foreclosure is pending or after judgment, no other action to recover any part of the mortgage debt without leave of court (RPAPL 1301(3)). The nonjudicial commercial power-of-sale procedure (RPAPL art. 14) expired July 1, 2009 per Approved Fin. Corp. v Dragonhearth Realty, 2010 NY Slip Op 20054.
deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency = amount owing under the judgment with interest + prior liens with interest + costs, disbursements and referee's fee, LESS the higher of the court-determined fair and reasonable market value (as of the auction date) or the sale price.
deficiency.timeLimit: Motion for leave to enter a deficiency judgment must be made simultaneously with the motion to confirm the sale, within 90 days after consummation of the sale by delivery of the deed; otherwise the sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction and no deficiency may be recovered in any action.

secondReading.notes: Statute text read on nysenate.gov. PREJUDGMENT: mandatory on a contract breach ('Interest shall be recovered', CPLR 5001(a)); discretionary as to rate and date only in actions of an equitable nature. 9% is CPLR 5004's rate (the 2% consumer-debt rate added by the 2022 amendment applies only to consumer debt with a natural-person defendant). Simple interest per In re RMM Records & Video Corp. (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 2007) applying CPLR 5004. CONTRACT RATE: 'when a contract provides for interest to be paid at a specified rate until the principal is paid, the contract rate of interest, rather than the legal rate set forth in C.P.L.R. 5004, governs until payment of the principal or until the contract is merged in a judgment' (Citibank v. Liebowitz, 110 A.D.2d 615 (2d Dep't 1985), quoted in In re RMM Records, Bankr. S.D.N.Y.); if the note is silent on a post-maturity/default rate, the contract rate runs to maturity and 9% thereafter (Brady v. Zambrana, 633 N.Y.S.2d 139 (1st Dep't 1995), as quoted there). POINTER CORRECTION: J. D'Addario & Co. v. Embassy Indus., 20 N.Y.3d 113 (2012) is about whether a contract's sole-remedy/liquidated-damages clause displaces CPLR 5001 statutory interest; it is not authority for the contract-rate rule. Whether a contract rate can be made to run after judgment by a clear post-judgment provision was not verified from a court source, so the output states the default merger rule only. FEES: no reciprocal statute for commercial contracts found after searching; RPL 234 (implied reciprocal tenant fees) applies only to 'a lease of residential property', and GOL 5-327 (implied reciprocal fees) applies only to consumer contracts with a natural person for personal, family or household purposes. No general contract fee statute found. DEFICIENCY: judicial foreclosure is the only live route; the FMV offset applies to every RPAPL 1371 deficiency.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Rate per R.C. 5703.47: federal short-term rate (26 U.S.C. 1274, for July of the current year) as determined by the Tax Commissioner on Oct. 15, rounded to the nearest whole percent, plus 3%; applies to interest accruing during the following calendar year. 2026 rate = 7% (Ohio Dept. of Taxation certified rate for 'all other taxes', 2026). The 2027 rate will be set on or about Oct. 15, 2026. Prejudgment interest accruing across several calendar years uses each year's rate.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the money becomes due and payable (R.C. 1343.03(A)).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Ohio Rev. Code 1343.03(A); 5703.47

postjudgmentInterest.formula: R.C. 5703.47 rate in effect on the date the judgment is rendered (2026: 7%), fixed for the life of the judgment until satisfied (R.C. 1343.03(B)); if the underlying written contract provides a different rate, that rate applies (R.C. 1343.03(A)).

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: R.C. 1319.02: a contractual commitment to pay attorneys' fees in a non-consumer 'contract of indebtedness' (expressly including a note, mortgage, and lease) is enforceable after maturity/default only if the total amount owed at the time the contract was entered into exceeded $100,000, and only in a reasonable amount. It enforces the clause as written; it does not make a one-sided clause reciprocal and does not award fees absent a clause.
feeShifting.citation: Ohio Rev. Code 1319.02

deficiency.timeLimit: No deficiency-specific time limit for commercial property. R.C. 2329.08 makes a deficiency on a judgment unenforceable 2 years after confirmation of the judicial sale, but only for mortgages on property with a dwelling for not more than two families used as a home/farm dwelling/homestead/homesite (waivable in writing).
deficiency.citation: Ohio Rev. Code 2329.08 (residential-only limit)

OH.notes: Ohio foreclosure is judicial; the money judgment on the note is normally entered in the foreclosure action and the deficiency is the unpaid balance after the sheriff's sale is confirmed. No Ohio statute limits a commercial deficiency to debt minus fair market value (fmvLimit null = no statutory FMV limit found, not unverified). reciprocalStatute null = no Ohio statute making one-sided fee clauses reciprocal was found. Compounding: R.C. 1343.03/5703.47 prescribe a per-annum rate and do not provide for compounding; a contract rate that compounds would govern under 1343.03(A). 1343.03(C) (good-faith-settlement prejudgment interest) applies only to tort actions.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: R.C. 5703.47 rate: federal short-term rate (26 U.S.C. 1274, for July of the current year) determined by the Tax Commissioner on October 15, rounded to the nearest whole percent, plus 3%; applies to interest accruing during the following calendar year. 2026 value: 7% (ODT Administrative Journal Entry, Oct. 15, 2025; July 2025 rounded FSTR 4% + 3%).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: R.C. 5703.47 (text as quoted in Ohio Dept. of Taxation Administrative Journal Entry dated Oct. 15, 2025); R.C. 1343.03(A) linkage NOT verified from statute text

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Same R.C. 5703.47 formula (2026 = 7%) -- application to judgments via R.C. 1343.03(A)/(B) NOT verified from statute text

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 23 O.S. 6: a party entitled to damages certain, or capable of being made certain by calculation, with the right vested on a particular day, recovers interest from that day. Rate = the 6% legal rate of 15 O.S. 266 absent a contract rate (applied to 23 O.S. 6 interest in Cable v. State ex rel. Okla. Police Pension & Ret. Bd., 2001 OK CIV APP 99, 31 P.3d 392, 399 n.11, and federal cases collected in Potter v. Synerlink Corp., No. 4:08-cv-674 (N.D. Okla. May 25, 2011)). The variable T-bill prejudgment rate in 12 O.S. 727.1(E),(I) (4.13% for 2026) applies only to personal-injury / injury-to-personal-rights verdicts, not contract claims.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: The particular day the right to recover the liquidated sum vested (e.g., each rent installment's due date / date the note amount became due), except while the debtor is prevented by law or by the creditor's act from paying (23 O.S. 6).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 12 O.S. 727.1(I): prime rate as listed in the first Wall Street Journal edition of each calendar year, certified by the State Treasurer in January, plus 2%; certified by the Administrative Director of the Courts (2026: 8.75%, per AOC notice of Jan. 2, 2026). The rate floats: each calendar year the judgment remains unpaid bears that year's rate, applied to the original judgment (including prejudgment interest) plus postjudgment interest previously accrued, i.e., compounds annually (727.1(C)). A contract rate, if specified, applies instead and is stated in the journal entry (727.1(D)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: 12 O.S. 727.1(A)-(D), (I); AOC Notice re Interest on Judgments (2026)

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: 12 O.S. 936(A): in a civil action to recover for labor or services rendered, or on an open account, statement of account, account stated, note, bill, negotiable instrument, or contract relating to the purchase or sale of goods, wares, or merchandise, the prevailing party (either side) is allowed a reasonable attorney fee taxed as costs, unless otherwise provided by law or by the contract sued on. A suit on a commercial promissory note is within the statute; a lease of real property is not among the enumerated categories on the statute's face.

deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial foreclosure: deficiency = amount owing with interest, plus costs and prior liens, less the HIGHER of the court-determined fair and reasonable market value (as of the sale date) or the sale price (12 O.S. 686). Power-of-sale foreclosure of non-homestead property: deficiency reduced by the amount, if any, by which fair market value on the sale date exceeded the sale price, if the mortgagor establishes it (46 O.S. 43(A)(2)(d)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Judicial: motion for a post-judgment deficiency order must be made with the motion to confirm sale or in any event within 90 days after the sale; otherwise the sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction and no deficiency is recoverable (12 O.S. 686). Power of sale (non-homestead): deficiency action must be commenced within 90 days after the date of sale (46 O.S. 43(A)(2)(d)).

OK.notes: reciprocalStatute null: no Oklahoma statute making a one-sided contractual fee clause reciprocal was found; 12 O.S. 936 itself is a two-way prevailing-party statute for its enumerated action types. 12 O.S. 686 also gives a defendant sued on a mortgage-secured debt outside foreclosure a set-off for the property's fair market value less prior liens. Prejudgment 6% rate is from case law applying 15 O.S. 266 to 23 O.S. 6 (Oklahoma Court of Civil Appeals and N.D./W.D. Okla. decisions), not from 23 O.S. 6's text itself. 2026 figures are from the Administrative Office of the Courts notice on OSCN.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the particular day the right to recover damages certain (or capable of being made certain by calculation) vests, i.e. the due date/breach date; not while the debtor is prevented by law or by the creditor's act from paying
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 23 O.S. 6 (right to interest on damages certain); 15 O.S. 266 (legal rate 6% absent contract rate)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate as listed in the first Wall Street Journal edition of the calendar year, certified by the State Treasurer to the Administrative Director of the Courts in January, plus 2%; recomputed each calendar year the judgment is unpaid (applies to prior accrued interest too). If a contract specifies a rate, that rate applies post-judgment and is stated in the journal entry (not above the lawful rate). 2026 rate: 8.75% (Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: 12 O.S. 727.1(A), (C), (D), (I); OSCN Notice re Interest on Judgments, Jan. 2, 2026

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: 12 O.S. 936(A): prevailing party (either side) gets a reasonable fee, taxed as costs, in actions to recover for labor or services, or on an open account, statement of account, account stated, note, bill, negotiable instrument, or contract for purchase/sale of goods -- 'unless otherwise provided by law or the contract.' Covers suits on a commercial promissory note; a commercial lease is not a listed category.

deficiency.allowed: Judicial foreclosure: allowed only on a motion for a post-judgment deficiency order filed with the motion to confirm sale or within 90 days after the sale; otherwise sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction (12 O.S. 686). Power-of-sale (nonjudicial) foreclosure of a non-homestead mortgage: mortgagor liable for deficiency unless otherwise agreed; action must be commenced within 90 days after the sale (46 O.S. 43(A)(2)(d)). Homestead election against deficiency under 46 O.S. 43(A)(2)(c) is residential-only and does not apply to commercial property.
deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial: deficiency = debt + interest + costs + prior liens, less the HIGHER of court-determined fair and reasonable market value at the sale date or the sale price (12 O.S. 686). Power of sale: if mortgagor proves FMV at sale date exceeded sale price, deficiency reduced by the excess (46 O.S. 43(A)(2)(d)). Separate suit on the note (not foreclosure) for a debt secured solely by the mortgage: defendant may set off FMV less prior liens (12 O.S. 686).
deficiency.timeLimit: 90 days after the sale (both judicial motion and power-of-sale action)

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest on a contract claim runs under 23 O.S. 6 at the 6% legal rate of 15 O.S. 266 unless the contract sets a rate ('in the absence of any contract as to the rate'). Neither statute states simple vs compound, so compounding is null. POINTER CORRECTION: 12 O.S. 727.1's prejudgment interest (average prior-year T-bill rate; 2026 = 4.13%) applies only to personal-injury / injury-to-personal-rights verdicts (727.1(E)) and lien-establishment judgments with no rate (727.1(H)) -- NOT to contract claims. Postjudgment formula is prime (first WSJ edition of year) + 2%, not 'first business day of December.' 2026 published values (OSCN notice Jan 2, 2026, effective Jan 1-Dec 31, 2026): postjudgment 8.75%, 727.1 prejudgment 4.13%. Fees: no Oklahoma statute found that converts a one-sided contractual fee clause into a reciprocal one (searched; 12 O.S. 936 is a category-limited prevailing-party statute, not a reciprocity statute). Residential lease fee-clause prohibitions are residential-only and do not apply. The pointer '12 O.S. 940' was not needed/verified (it concerns damage-to-property actions).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 9% per annum on all moneys after they become due, if the parties have not otherwise agreed to a rate (ORS 82.010(1)(a)); open accounts bear interest from the date of the last item.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the money becomes due (ORS 82.010(1)(a)); for an open account, the date of the last item.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 9% per annum simple (unless otherwise provided by contract) from entry of judgment unless the judgment specifies another date; also accrues on prejudgment interest included in the judgment and on fees/costs in the judgment. A judgment on a contract bearing MORE than 9% bears the contract rate (ORS 82.010(2)(a)-(e)).

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: ORS 20.096(1): where a contract (including any instrument evidencing a debt) specifically provides that fees and costs to enforce it shall be awarded to one party, the party that prevails on the claim is entitled to reasonable attorney fees regardless of whether it is the party specified in the contract; fee-waiver provisions in contracts entered after Sept. 9, 1971 are void (20.096(2)).
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: ORS 20.082: absent a contractual fee clause, the prevailing party on a contract claim (including an instrument evidencing a debt) recovers reasonable attorney fees only if principal plus interest due when the claim is filed is $10,000 or less; plaintiff must have made written demand at least 20 days before filing, and no fees to plaintiff if defendant tendered at least the amount awarded.

deficiency.timeLimit: No deficiency-specific deadline found for commercial judicial foreclosure; the deficiency must be requested in the complaint (ORS 86.797(3)) and is part of the foreclosure judgment.

OR.notes: Deficiency: BARRED after any nonjudicial trustee's sale (commercial or residential) and after judicial foreclosure of a residential trust deed (ORS 86.797(2)). ALLOWED after judicial foreclosure of a non-residential (commercial) trust deed: judgment may provide execution for the amount by which the money award exceeds net sale proceeds, if the plaintiff requested it in the complaint (ORS 86.797(3)); an action against a guarantor for a deficiency after judicial foreclosure is not precluded (86.797(4)(b)). For mortgages (not trust deeds), deficiency remedies expire at sale if the mortgage was given to a SELLER to secure the unpaid purchase price (ORS 88.103(1)(a), not limited to residential property). fmvLimit null: no Oregon statute limiting a commercial deficiency to debt minus fair market value was found. Deficiency 'allowed' = true only for judicial foreclosure of a commercial trust deed/mortgage that is not a seller purchase-money mortgage. Prejudgment compounding: ORS 82.010(1) states a per-annum rate without compounding; only 82.010(2)(b) expressly says judgment interest is simple, so 'simple' for prejudgment is the statute's plain reading, not separately verified in case law.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: On all moneys after they become due (open accounts: from the date of the last item)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 9% per annum simple interest from entry of judgment (unless judgment specifies another date or contract provides otherwise); also accrues on pre-judgment interest and on fees/costs in the judgment. A judgment on a contract bearing more than 9% bears the contract rate.

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: ORS 20.096(1): where a contract provides that fees incurred to enforce it shall be awarded to one party, the party that prevails on the contract claim gets reasonable fees regardless of whether it is the party named in the clause; ORS 20.096(2): fee rights may not be waived (waiver clauses void) for contracts entered after Sept. 9, 1971. 'Contract' includes any instrument evidencing a debt (20.096(3)).
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: ORS 20.082: court shall award reasonable fees to the prevailing party on a contract claim only if principal plus interest due at filing is $10,000 or less AND the contract has no fee clause (small-claim rule; rarely relevant to commercial lease/loan claims).

deficiency.allowed: Trustee's sale (nonjudicial) of any trust deed, commercial or residential: deficiency action barred (ORS 86.797(2)). Judicial foreclosure of a NON-residential trust deed: allowed -- judgment with money award must provide for execution on the unpaid balance after net sale proceeds if plaintiff requests it in the complaint (ORS 86.797(3)). Judicial foreclosure of a residential trust deed: barred. Mortgages: deficiency allowed except purchase-money mortgages to sellers and certain small residential purchase-money mortgages (ORS 88.103). Guarantor deficiency after judicial foreclosure preserved (86.797(4)(b)).

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment: ORS 82.010(1) sets 9% 'if the parties have not otherwise agreed to a rate of interest', so a lease/note rate displaces it. The statute does not say simple or compound for prejudgment interest (82.010(2)(b) 'simple interest, unless otherwise provided by contract' applies to judgment interest), so compounding left null. Oregon courts generally limit prejudgment interest to amounts ascertainable/liquidated as of a date -- that is case law not verified from a court source here, so not cited. ORS 82.010(3) caps interest on business/agricultural loans of $50,000 or less (greater of 12% or 5% over the Fed 90-day commercial paper discount rate) -- not relevant to larger commercial loans. fmvLimit null: no fair-value offset statute found in ORS 86.797/88.103 (text read). timeLimit null: no deficiency-specific filing deadline found in those sections; ordinary limitations periods apply. Pointer corrections: ORS 88.070 was renumbered 88.103 in 2013; the pointer 'no deficiency after trustee's sale; exceptions for commercial?' -- there is NO commercial exception for trustee's sales; the commercial route is judicial foreclosure under 86.797(3).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Legal rate of 6% per annum (41 P.S. 202) where the contract specifies no rate. Pennsylvania grants prejudgment interest on a breach-of-contract claim as a matter of right where the sum is definite or ascertainable (Fernandez v. Levin, 519 Pa. 375, 548 A.2d 1191, 1193 (1988)); this entitlement is case law, not a statute.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the amount due under the contract was initially withheld, i.e., the due date of each unpaid sum (Travelers Cas. & Sur. Co. v. Ins. Co. of N. Am., 609 F.3d 143, 172 (3d Cir. 2010), applying Pennsylvania law).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 41 P.S. 202; Fernandez v. Levin, 548 A.2d 1191 (Pa. 1988)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment for a specific sum bears interest at the 'lawful rate' (6% under 41 P.S. 202) from the date of the verdict or award, or from the date of judgment if not entered on a verdict or award, except as otherwise provided by another statute (42 Pa.C.S. 8101).

feeShifting.citation: 42 Pa.C.S. 2503 (exclusive list of fee-entitled participants; no general contract category)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency Judgment Act: when real property is sold, directly or indirectly, to the judgment creditor in execution proceedings for less than the judgment, interest and costs, the creditor must petition the court to fix fair market value; the debtor is released to the extent of the court-fixed fair market value less prior liens, costs, taxes and municipal claims not discharged by the sale (special allocation rules for nonconsumer creditors in 8103(f)). Waivers of the Act's protection are void (8103(e)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Petition to fix fair market value / establish the deficiency must be filed within 6 months after execution and delivery of the sheriff's deed (42 Pa.C.S. 5522(b)(2)); if not, the debtor, guarantor or other liable party may have the judgment marked satisfied (8103(d)).

PA.notes: feeShifting all null: no Pennsylvania statute making one-sided contractual fee clauses reciprocal, and no general statute awarding fees on commercial contract claims, was found; Pennsylvania follows the American Rule, so fees on a commercial lease/loan claim come only from the contract clause itself. Whether a note/lease contract rate also governs POST-judgment interest (displacing the 6% lawful rate) was not verified from statute; 8101 says only 'lawful rate ... except as otherwise provided by another statute'. The 8103 FMV procedure is triggered when the property is sold to the judgment creditor (directly or indirectly). Prejudgment 'matter of right' rule and accrual date come from case law (Fernandez; Travelers, as quoted in Domus BWW Funding, LLC v. Arch Ins. Co., No. 2:23-cv-00094 (E.D. Pa. Oct. 31, 2024)).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date each payment was due under the contract (Restatement (Second) of Contracts 354, adopted in Pennsylvania). For unaccelerated rent, from each installment's due date; where an anticipatory breach entitles the landlord to call the full balance due, from the breach date (Newman Dev. Grp. v. Genuardi's, 2013 PA Super 217).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 41 P.S. 202 (legal rate 6%); TruServ Corp. v. Morgan's Tool & Supply Co., 39 A.3d 253, 260-61 (Pa. 2012) (statutory prejudgment rate 6%; contractual vs prejudgment interest), as quoted in Newman Dev. Grp. of Pottstown, LLC v. Genuardi's Family Mkt., Inc., 2013 PA Super 217

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment for a specific sum bears interest 'at the lawful rate' from the date of verdict/award (or from judgment if not entered on a verdict/award), 'except as otherwise provided by another statute'; the lawful/legal rate is 6% per annum under 41 P.S. 202.

feeShifting.citation: 42 Pa.C.S. 2503 (exclusive list of fee-entitled participants; no general contract category)

deficiency.fmvLimit: When the property is sold directly or indirectly to the judgment creditor at the execution (sheriff's) sale and the price does not satisfy the judgment, the creditor must petition the court to fix fair market value; the debtor is discharged to the extent of FMV (less prior liens, costs, taxes and municipal claims not discharged by the sale). Waivers of the Act are void. Special allocation rules for nonconsumer creditors on partial-recourse or partially guaranteed obligations (8103(f)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Petition to fix FMV must be filed within six months after execution and delivery of the sheriff's deed (42 Pa.C.S. 5522(b)(2)); if not, debtor/guarantor may petition to have the judgment marked satisfied (8103(d)).
deficiency.citation: 42 Pa.C.S. 8103 (Deficiency Judgment Act); 42 Pa.C.S. 5522(b)(2)

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest on a contract claim is governed by case law (Restatement (Second) of Contracts 354 as adopted in Pa.), at the 6% legal rate of 41 P.S. 202; availability/rate verified from the Superior Court's Newman opinion (pacourts.us), which quotes TruServ (Pa. 2012): statutory prejudgment rate is 6%, and a party may recover contractual interest OR prejudgment interest, not both for the same period -- so a lease/note default rate controls when the contract provides one. The commonly repeated 'as of right' characterization and the no-compounding rule (Restatement 354 comment) were NOT verified from a court text in this pass, so compounding is null. Pointer note: Fernandez v. Levin, 519 Pa. 375, 548 A.2d 1191 (1988) is a Pa. Supreme Court case (bounced-check assumpsit), cited in TruServ; not independently read. Postjudgment: whether a contract default rate carries into the judgment was not verified (8101 says 'except as otherwise provided by another statute' and does not mention contracts), so treated as 6% statutory. Fees: Pennsylvania follows the American Rule; 42 Pa.C.S. 2503 lists fee-entitled participants and has no general contract-claim category; no statute found making one-sided fee clauses reciprocal (searched). Contractual fee clauses are enforced as written. Act 6 (41 P.S. 406, 503) fee limits apply only to residential mortgages. Deficiency: Pennsylvania has no nonjudicial power-of-sale foreclosure, so the only route is judicial (mortgage foreclosure/execution); 8103 applies whenever the property is sold directly or indirectly to the judgment creditor. 41 P.S. 201's 6% usury ceiling does not apply to business loans or obligations over $50,000.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 12% per annum on pecuniary damages in any civil action in which a verdict is rendered or decision made, added by the clerk, from the date the cause of action accrued (R.I. Gen. Laws 9-21-10(a)). Mandatory (added by the clerk), not discretionary. Does not apply 'to any contractual obligation where interest is already provided'.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date the cause of action accrued (for unpaid rent / a note, the date of breach/nonpayment of each sum).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws 9-21-10(a)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 12% per annum to the time of discharge (9-21-8); under 9-21-10(a) post-judgment interest accrues at 12% on both the principal amount of the judgment and the prejudgment interest included in it.

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: R.I. Gen. Laws 9-1-45: in any civil action arising from a breach of contract, the court MAY award a reasonable attorney's fee to the prevailing party only if it (1) finds a complete absence of a justiciable issue of law or fact raised by the losing party, or (2) renders a default judgment against the losing party. Discretionary and limited to those two situations.
feeShifting.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws 9-1-45

deficiency.citation: Boucher v. Sweet, 147 A.3d 71 (R.I. 2016) (mortgagee recovered deficiency on note in separate action after power-of-sale foreclosure); R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 34-27 contains no deficiency bar

RI.notes: reciprocalStatute null: no Rhode Island statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal was found. Deficiency: Rhode Island has no anti-deficiency or fair-market-value statute for commercial mortgages (chapter 34-27, Mortgage Foreclosure and Sale, has none); the deficiency is pursued by a separate action on the note after the (typically nonjudicial power-of-sale) foreclosure, where the borrower may contest the propriety of the sale (Boucher v. Sweet). fmvLimit null = none found. timeLimit null: no deficiency-specific deadline found; the general limitations period for an action on the note would govern, which was not verified here. Boucher v. Sweet, 147 A.3d 71 (R.I. Oct. 28, 2016), confirmed via Justia/CourtListener listings; residential property in that case, but no statute distinguishes commercial property. Prejudgment compounding: 9-21-10 states a flat per-annum rate added by the clerk; treated as simple.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date the cause of action accrued (added by the clerk to the verdict/decision for pecuniary damages and included in the judgment); mandatory, not discretionary
prejudgmentInterest.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-21-10(a)

postjudgmentInterest.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-21-8; § 9-21-10(a) (post-judgment 12% accrues on principal and the prejudgment interest)

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-45: court MAY award a reasonable attorney's fee to the prevailing party in any civil action arising from a breach of contract only if it (1) finds a complete absence of a justiciable issue of law or fact raised by the losing party, or (2) renders a default judgment against the losing party. Discretionary; not a general loser-pays rule.
feeShifting.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-45

deficiency.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 34-27 (Mortgage Foreclosure and Sale) — contains no anti-deficiency, fair-value, or deficiency time-limit provision

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment: § 9-21-10(a) text: 'This section shall not apply until entry of judgment or to any contractual obligation where interest is already provided' — so a lease/note interest rate displaces the 12% statutory rate (contractRateControls true). Statute does not provide for compounding of prejudgment interest (simple); post-judgment 12% runs on principal plus prejudgment interest. Subsection (b) (medical malpractice accrual) not relevant. Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute found after searching; one-sided contractual fee clauses are governed by ordinary contract law. § 9-1-45 is discretionary and limited to no-justiciable-issue or default cases. Deficiency: RI has no statute barring or limiting deficiency judgments; the foreclosure chapter (34-27, section index checked: 34-27-1 through 34-27-9) has no deficiency, fair-market-value-offset, or time-limit section, so deficiency recovery on the note is by separate action under ordinary contract law (fmvLimit and timeLimit null for that reason). The general civil limitations period is 10 years after accrual (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-13(a), https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE9/9-1/9-1-13.htm), but no deficiency-specific limit was found; a sealed/UCC instrument may carry a different period — not researched. Non-judicial power-of-sale foreclosure is the usual method (§ 34-27-4); judicial foreclosure by complaint under § 34-27-1. The § 34-27-9 mediation requirement applies only to owner-occupied 1-4 unit residential primary residences, not commercial.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 8.75% per annum 'in all cases of accounts stated and in all cases wherein any sum or sums of money shall be ascertained and, being due, shall draw interest according to law' (S.C. Code 34-31-20(A)). Applies to a sum certain or capable of being reduced to certainty; a contractual rate displaces it (Bickerstaff v. Prevost, S.C. Ct. App. Op. No. 4439 (2008, refiled Jan. 7, 2009), affirming prejudgment interest at the contract rate).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the ascertained sum became due (34-31-20(A)).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: S.C. Code Ann. 34-31-20(A); Bickerstaff v. Prevost, Op. No. 4439 (S.C. Ct. App. 2009)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate in the first Wall Street Journal edition of each calendar year plus 4 percentage points, compounded annually; confirmed by Supreme Court order by Jan. 15 each year (34-31-20(B)). For Jan. 15, 2026 - Jan. 14, 2027: 6.75% + 4 = 10.75% compounded annually (S.C. Sup. Ct. Order 2026-01-07-01). A lawful contract rate fixed for after maturity applies to a judgment on that contract instead (Turner Coleman, Inc. v. Ohio Constr. & Eng'g, Inc., 272 S.C. 289, 251 S.E.2d 738 (1979), as quoted in Bickerstaff v. Prevost, Op. No. 4972 (S.C. Ct. App. 2012)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: S.C. Code Ann. 34-31-20(B); S.C. Sup. Ct. Order dated Jan. 7, 2026

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (S.C. follows the American rule; contractual fee clauses enforced as written)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Statutory appraisal: a defendant against whom a personal judgment is taken or asked may, within 30 days after the foreclosure sale, petition for appraisal of the property's true value as of the sale date by three appraisers; the deficiency is abated by the amount the appraised value exceeds the sale price (extinguished entirely if that excess equals or exceeds the deficiency) (29-3-680 to -740). For non-dwelling, non-consumer transactions (i.e., commercial) the appraisal right is WAIVABLE by a pre-transaction written notice plus a signed statutory waiver statement (29-3-680(B)). Separately, 15-39-720 keeps bidding open until the 30th day after a judicial foreclosure sale for upset bids (interaction with deficiency waivers not verified).
deficiency.timeLimit: No separate deficiency action deadline; the deficiency is adjudged in the foreclosure action (29-3-660). The debtor's appraisal petition must be filed within 30 days after the sale (29-3-680(A)), extendable only by the judgment creditor's written consent (29-3-690).

SC.notes: South Carolina foreclosure is judicial; the court may adjudge the mortgagor (and guarantors made parties) liable for any residue after sale (29-3-660). Commercial loan documents frequently include the statutory appraisal waiver, in which case the high bid is applied to the debt regardless of appraised value; the calculator should ask whether a waiver was signed. feeShifting null: no South Carolina statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract-fee statute applicable to commercial lease/loan claims, was found; fees come from the contract clause. Prejudgment compounding: 34-31-20(A) states a per-annum rate without compounding (the 'compounded annually' language is only in subsection (B) for judgments).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: When the sum is ascertained and due (liquidated claim: sum certain or capable of being reduced to certainty; test is whether the measure of recovery was fixed by conditions existing when the claim arose). Not allowed on unliquidated claims absent agreement or statute.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 34-31-20(A); Butler Contracting, Inc. v. Court Street, LLC, 369 S.C. 121, 631 S.E.2d 252 (2006) and Smith-Hunter Constr. Co. v. Hopson, 365 S.C. 125, 616 S.E.2d 419 (2005), as quoted in S.C. Ct. App. Op. No. 4214

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Prime rate as listed in the first edition of the Wall Street Journal published for the calendar year, plus 4 percentage points, compounded annually; S.C. Supreme Court confirms by order by January 15 each year
postjudgmentInterest.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 34-31-20(B); S.C. Supreme Court Order 2026-01-07-01 (Jan. 7, 2026)

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (S.C. follows the American rule; contractual fee clauses enforced as written)

deficiency.allowed: Allowed; judicial foreclosure only (no power-of-sale). Court may adjudge payment of the residue of the mortgage debt after sale.
deficiency.fmvLimit: Appraisal right: a defendant against whom a personal (deficiency) judgment is taken or asked may, within 30 days after the sale, petition the clerk for an appraisal by three state-certified/licensed appraisers; if appraised value minus the sale price equals or exceeds the deficiency, the judgment is extinguished, otherwise it is reduced accordingly (§§ 29-3-680 to 29-3-760, esp. § 29-3-740). For non-dwelling (commercial) transactions the debtor may waive appraisal rights in advance by a signed statement containing the statutory waiver language (§ 29-3-680). Separately, when a deficiency is demanded, bidding stays open 30 days after the judicial sale for upset bids (§ 15-39-720; not applicable if the complaint waives deficiency, § 15-39-760).
deficiency.timeLimit: Deficiency is sought within the foreclosure action (§§ 29-3-650, 29-3-660); debtor's appraisal petition due within 30 days after the sale (§ 29-3-680), not enlargeable without the judgment creditor's written consent (§ 29-3-690). No separate deficiency-suit deadline found.

secondReading.notes: Pointer correction: the post-judgment rate is NOT set from the WSJ prime rate on the first business day of December; § 34-31-20(B) uses the prime rate listed in the first edition of the WSJ published for each calendar year, plus 4 points, compounded annually, confirmed by Supreme Court order by Jan 15. Current value: Order 2026-01-07-01 — WSJ Jan. 2, 2026 prime 6.75%, so 10.75% compounded annually for January 15, 2026 through January 14, 2027. Prejudgment: § 34-31-20(A) fixes 8.75% per annum for accounts stated and sums ascertained and due; the statute is silent on compounding (only subsection (B) judgment interest compounds), so simple. Availability rule (liquidated/sum-certain) is case law, verified from the S.C. Court of Appeals' own opinion No. 4214 on sccourts.org (https://www.sccourts.org/media/opinions/HTMLFiles/COA/4214.htm) quoting Butler Contracting and Smith-Hunter. contractRateControls null: § 34-31-20 contains no contract-rate provision and I could not verify from statute or a court source whether a lease/note rate displaces 8.75% pre-judgment or carries into the judgment (a law-firm chart says the contract rate applies both pre- and post-judgment, but that is secondary and unverified). Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract fee-shifting statute found after searching; § 15-36-10 (Frivolous Civil Proceedings Sanctions Act) exists but is a sanctions statute, not contract fee-shifting (not separately verified). Deficiency: § 29-3-630 requires the debt be established by court judgment before a mortgage sale passes title, i.e., judicial foreclosure only; § 29-3-670 says the deficiency is not extinguished by the mortgagee buying at the sale.

resolutions: contract rate controls per the second reading's case-law source; first reading found only a secondary source; medium confidence

prejudgmentInterest.formula: A person entitled to recover damages is entitled to interest from the day the loss or damage occurred (SDCL 21-1-13.1). On contract damages: the contract rate if the contract so provides; otherwise the Category B rate of SDCL 54-3-16 = 10% per year. Court computes and includes it in the judgment. Not recoverable on future, punitive, or intangible damages.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Day the loss or damage occurred (e.g., each missed rent/loan payment); if disputed, the date specified in the verdict or decision; runs through the verdict date (or judgment entry if no verdict); suspended while the debtor is prevented by law or by the creditor's act from paying.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Category B rate (10% per year, SDCL 54-3-16(2)) on all judgments from and after the date of judgment (SDCL 54-3-5.1); interest from verdict/decision to entry of judgment is added to the judgment (SDCL 15-16-3).

feeShifting.citation: SDCL 15-17-38 (fees left to the parties' agreement; taxable as disbursements only if allowed by specific statute; fees may be taxed as disbursements on mortgage foreclosures by action or advertisement)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial foreclosure (by action): if the mortgagee will not bid the full judgment debt, it must prove the fair and reasonable value of the premises at trial; the court fixes that value in the decree and may authorize the mortgagee to bid not less than that value less prior liens/taxes; a deficiency general execution then issues only on application to the court (SDCL 21-47-16). Nonjudicial sale (by advertisement/power of sale) where the mortgagee or holder buys: before any deficiency judgment the holder must prove the property sold for its true market value or more, and the court deducts from the deficiency any shortfall of the sale price below true market value (SDCL 21-48-14; does not apply to court-ordered sales).

SD.notes: feeShifting reciprocal/general null: no South Dakota statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract-claim fee statute, was found; SDCL 15-17-38 states fees are left to the parties' agreement and taxed only where a specific statute allows (foreclosures are one such case). deficiency.timeLimit null: no deficiency-specific deadline was found in SDCL 21-47-16 or 21-48-14; not researched further. Post-judgment: SDCL 54-3-5.1 does not say whether a contract rate displaces Category B on a judgment on a note/lease; not verified. The SD alternative 'short-term redemption'/small-tract procedures were not reviewed.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the day the loss or damage occurred (e.g., breach/due date), except while the debtor is prevented by law or by act of the creditor from paying; if disputed, from the date specified in the verdict/decision, running through the verdict date (or judgment date if no verdict). Court computes and includes it in the judgment.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: SDCL § 21-1-13.1; SDCL § 54-3-16 (Category B = 10% per year)

postjudgmentInterest.citation: SDCL § 54-3-5.1 (judgments bear Category B rate from date of judgment); SDCL § 54-3-16 (Category B = 10% per year)

deficiency.allowed: Judicial foreclosure (by action): foreclosure is a complete satisfaction of the debt (§ 21-47-17) UNLESS the mortgagee, unwilling to bid the full judgment debt, proves at trial the fair and reasonable value, the decree authorizes a bid of not less than that value (less prior liens), and a deficiency remains — then general execution for the deficiency only on application to the court (§ 21-47-16). Foreclosure by advertisement (power of sale): deficiency allowed, but if the mortgagee/holder bought at the sale it must first prove to the court that the property sold for its true market value or more, and the court deducts any shortfall between true market value and the sale price (§ 21-48-14).
deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial: minimum bid set at court-determined fair and reasonable value (less prior liens) as a precondition to any deficiency (§§ 21-47-15, 21-47-16). Power of sale where mortgagee buys: deficiency reduced by the difference between true market value at the time of sale and the sale price (§ 21-48-14).

secondReading.notes: Pointer check: 21-1-13.1, 54-3-16 (Category B = 10%) and 54-3-5.1 confirmed. Prejudgment: § 21-1-13.1 says prejudgment interest on contract damages 'shall be at the contract rate, if so provided in the contract; otherwise, if prejudgment interest is awarded, it shall be at the Category B rate' — contractRateControls true. Excludes future, punitive and intangible damages. Statute gives an annual rate and is silent on compounding (simple). Post-judgment: § 54-3-5.1 applies the Category B 10% rate to all judgments (it does not provide for a contract rate carrying into the judgment). Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract fee-shifting statute found. IMPORTANT restriction: SDCL § 15-17-39 makes any provision in a 'note, bond, mortgage, or other evidence of debt' providing for attorneys' fees on default or foreclosure 'against public policy and void, except as authorized by specific statute'; § 15-17-38 leaves compensation to agreement but allows fees to be taxed only where allowed by specific statute, and expressly allows fees as disbursements on mortgage foreclosures by action or advertisement (see also § 21-48-15). So a commercial loan's contractual fee clause is generally unenforceable outside foreclosure; whether § 15-17-39 reaches a commercial lease fee clause (a lease is not obviously an 'evidence of debt') was not verified. § 15-17-51 (frivolous/malicious claims) is a sanctions statute, not contract fee-shifting. Deficiency timeLimit null: no deficiency-specific deadline found in chs. 21-47/21-48 (§ 21-48-14 section list checked); § 21-48-14 does not apply to court-ordered sales or foreclosures by action. Assignment-of-rents agreements survive a judicial foreclosure (§ 21-47-17).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Discretionary: may be awarded by courts or juries in accordance with the principles of equity at any rate not in excess of a maximum effective rate of 10% per annum (for contracts subject to T.C.A. 47-14-103, the maximum is that section's rate for the transaction category). 'rate' = the 10% statutory MAXIMUM, not a default. Award is within the trial court's sound discretion, guided by whether it would be fair considering all the facts (Myint v. Allstate Ins. Co., 970 S.W.2d 920 (Tenn. 1998)). Contracts may expressly provide the same or a different post-breach/default rate within 47-14-103 limits.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Not fixed by statute; set by the court in its equitable discretion (typically from when the amount became due/was wrongfully withheld).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. 47-14-123; Myint v. Allstate Ins. Co., 970 S.W.2d 920 (Tenn. 1998)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 2% less than the 'formula rate' published by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions under 47-14-105: for judgments entered Jan. 1-June 30, the December prior-year formula rate; for judgments entered July 1-Dec. 31, the June formula rate (47-14-121(a)). Fixed at entry for the life of the judgment. AOC-published rate: 8.75% for judgments entered 1/1/2026-6/30/2026 and 7/1/2026-12/31/2026. Where the judgment is based on a note, contract or other writing fixing a rate within 47-14-103 limits, the judgment bears that rate (47-14-121(c)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. 47-14-121; Tennessee AOC, Tennessee Judgment Interest Rates

feeShifting.citation: No statute found; American rule — Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. v. Epperson, No. M2006-02424-SC-R11-CV (Tenn. 2009) (fees recoverable only where contract or statute specifically and expressly provides)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency = total indebtedness before sale plus foreclosure/sale costs, less the fair market value at the time of sale. Rebuttable presumption that the sale price equals fair market value; the debtor overcomes it by proving by a preponderance that the property sold for an amount materially less than FMV, in which case the court-determined FMV is credited (absent fraud, collusion, misconduct or irregularity in the sale) (35-5-117(b)-(c)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action must be brought by the earlier of (A) 2 years after the trustee's or foreclosure sale (excluding time a bankruptcy petition is pending) or (B) the time for enforcing the indebtedness under 28-1-102 and 28-2-111 (35-5-117(d)(1)). Creditor may instead sue on the debt before, with, or in lieu of foreclosure (35-5-117(d)(2)).
deficiency.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. 35-5-117

TN.notes: Tennessee statute text read from Justia (mirror; official code is hosted by LexisNexis). feeShifting all null: no Tennessee statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general statute awarding fees on commercial contract claims, was found; Tennessee follows the American Rule, so fees come only from the lease/loan clause. Prejudgment compounding: 47-14-123 caps the 'effective rate' per annum and does not authorize compounding; the calculator should treat it as simple unless the contract provides otherwise (not separately verified in case law). For the calculator, TN prejudgment interest is a discretionary award up to the cap, so it should be presented as a possible range (0% to 10%, or the contract post-default rate) rather than a certain amount.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Court or jury may award in accordance with principles of equity at any rate not exceeding a maximum effective rate of 10% per annum; for contracts subject to § 47-14-103 the maximum is the rate set by that section for the category of transaction; a contract may expressly set the same or a different post-breach/default rate within § 47-14-103 limits
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Set by the court in its equitable discretion (not fixed by statute). Myint: purpose is to compensate for loss of use of funds; allowed where the amount is ascertainable by computation or a recognized standard of valuation and the obligation is not disputed on reasonable grounds, though uncertainty does not mandate denial. In Myint the court ran interest from the claim denial date rather than the date of loss.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 47-14-123; Myint v. Allstate Ins. Co., 970 S.W.2d 920 (Tenn. 1998)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 2 percentage points below the formula rate published by the Tennessee Commissioner of Financial Institutions under § 47-14-105 — for judgments entered Jan 1-Jun 30, the December (prior year) formula rate; for judgments entered Jul 1-Dec 31, the June formula rate. Rate is fixed at entry and does not fluctuate. AOC publishes it each half-year. If the judgment is based on a note/contract/writing fixing a rate within § 47-14-103 limits, the judgment bears that contract rate (§ 47-14-121(c)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 47-14-121; Tennessee AOC, Tennessee Judgment Interest Rates

feeShifting.citation: No statute found; American rule — Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. v. Epperson, No. M2006-02424-SC-R11-CV (Tenn. 2009) (fees recoverable only where contract or statute specifically and expressly provides)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Deficiency = total indebtedness before sale + costs of foreclosure and sale − fair market value at time of sale (absent fraud, collusion, misconduct or irregularity). Creditor gets a rebuttable prima facie presumption that sale price = FMV; debtor rebuts by proving by a preponderance that the property sold for an amount materially less than FMV, in which case the court determines FMV and the deficiency is computed from it.
deficiency.timeLimit: Action must be brought by the earlier of (A) 2 years after the trustee's or foreclosure sale, excluding time a bankruptcy petition is pending, or (B) the time for enforcing the indebtedness under §§ 28-1-102 and 28-2-111. Creditor may instead sue on the debt before, during, or in lieu of foreclosure (§ 35-5-117(d)(2)).
deficiency.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 35-5-117

secondReading.notes: Pointer corrections: (1) § 47-14-121 is NOT '2 points below the Fed prime loan rate'; it is 2% below the formula rate published by the TN Commissioner of Financial Institutions (§ 47-14-105), using the prior December rate for Jan-Jun judgments and the June rate for Jul-Dec judgments, calculated and published by the AOC. (2) The deficiency statute is now § 35-5-117 (it appears as § 35-5-118 in the 2021 code; current § 35-5-118 concerns title 67 tax sales). Current post-judgment values from the AOC page (read in browser 2026-09-25): 8.75% for judgments entered on/after 7/1/2026; 8.75% for 1/1/2026-6/30/2026; 9.50% for 2025; the rate is fixed at entry. Prejudgment: discretionary/equitable, capped at 10% effective per annum (or the § 47-14-103 category rate for contracts subject to that section); rate left null because the court sets it within the cap. Compounding 'simple' reflects practice in Myint (trial court applied simple 10%) and the statute's 'maximum effective rate' cap; the statute does not itself mandate simple interest. contractRateControls true: § 47-14-123 lets a contract expressly provide a post-breach/default rate within § 47-14-103 limits, and § 47-14-121(c) carries a contract rate into the judgment. Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute or general contract fee statute found; contractual fee clauses are enforced only if they specifically and expressly provide for attorney fees (Cracker Barrel). Statute text read from FindLaw (current through Jan. 2, 2024 per the page) because law.justia.com blocked automated fetch and the official LexisNexis TN portal was not used; 2025-2026 session amendments not exhaustively checked (the AOC page confirms the § 47-14-121 formula is still applied in 2026). Haddon v. Vanlier (Tenn. May 12, 2026) addresses prejudgment interest in uninsured-motorist tort cases only — not relevant to contract claims.

resolutions: discretionary, capped at 10% (Tenn. Code 47-14-123); the 10% is a ceiling, not a rate

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Common-law (equitable) prejudgment interest on a breach-of-contract claim: 'The rate of prejudgment interest shall be the same as the rate of postjudgment interest at the time of judgment' (Johnson & Higgins v. Kenneco, 962 S.W.2d 507 (Tex. 1998), borrowing Fin. Code ch. 304 subch. B). That postjudgment rate is the Fin. Code 304.003(c) rate: Federal Reserve prime rate on the 15th of the month before judgment, floor 5%, cap 15%, set monthly by the consumer credit commissioner and published in the Texas Register.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Earlier of (1) 180 days after the defendant receives written notice of the claim or (2) the date suit is filed; runs to the day before judgment (Kenneco; mirrors Fin. Code 304.104).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Johnson & Higgins of Tex., Inc. v. Kenneco Energy, Inc., 962 S.W.2d 507 (Tex. 1998) (common law, applies to all judgments on or after Dec. 11, 1997, including breach of contract); Tex. Fin. Code 304.003, 304.103, 304.104 (statutory subchapter B itself applies only to wrongful death, personal injury, and property damage cases, per 304.101)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: If the judgment is on a contract that provides for interest: lesser of the contract rate (may be variable) or 18% a year (304.002). Otherwise: prime rate as published by the Federal Reserve Board, determined by the consumer credit commissioner on the 15th of each month for judgments rendered the following month; floor 5%, cap 15% (304.003). Accrues from rendition to satisfaction (304.005); compounds annually (304.006).

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 38.001(b)(8): a person may recover reasonable attorney's fees, in addition to the amount of a valid claim and costs, on a claim for an oral or written contract, from 'an individual or organization' (organization as defined in Bus. Orgs. Code 1.002, so LLCs and partnerships are covered after the 2021 amendment, H.B. 1578, eff.
