Sept. 1, 2021), except a quasi-governmental entity authorized by state law, a religious organization, a charitable organization, or a charitable trust. Procedure (38.002): claimant must be represented by an attorney, must present the claim, and the just amount must not be tendered within 30 days of presentment. Fee claimant must prevail and recover damages (case law, not stated in the statute).
feeShifting.citation: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 38.001, 38.002

deficiency.fmvLimit: Nonjudicial sale (Prop. Code 51.002): any person against whom a deficiency is sought may move for a determination of the property's fair market value as of the foreclosure date; if FMV exceeds the sale price, the obligors get an offset equal to FMV (less unextinguished liens) minus sale price; if no request or no competent evidence, the sale price is used (51.003(b)-(c)). Judicial foreclosure: obligors including guarantors may sue for the same FMV offset within 90 days after the sale (51.004).
deficiency.timeLimit: Action to recover a deficiency after a nonjudicial sale must be brought within two years of the foreclosure sale (51.003(a)).

TX.notes: Fin. Code ch. 304 subch. B (prejudgment interest) by its terms applies only to wrongful death, personal injury, and property damage cases (304.101); contract claims get prejudgment interest under Kenneco's common-law rule, which adopts the same rate, accrual, and simple-interest mechanics. contractRateControls left null for prejudgment interest: 304.002 makes the contract rate (capped at 18%) the POSTjudgment rate on a contract providing for interest, but I did not verify from a primary source a Texas Supreme Court holding that a contract rate displaces the Kenneco equitable rate for the PREjudgment period (contractual interest on a note or late-payment clause is generally recovered as contract damages, but that was not source-verified here). Official statute text is served at statutes.capitol.texas.gov (JavaScript app); the raw text was read from tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/{FI,CP,PR}/htm/. 38.001 was amended by H.B. 1578 eff. Sept. 1, 2021 (prior text allowed recovery only from 'an individual or corporation'); the amendment's transition clause was not verified here, so older cases may need the prior text.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Common law (Johnson & Higgins of Tex., Inc. v. Kenneco Energy, Inc., 962 S.W.2d 507 (Tex. 1998)): prejudgment interest on claims outside Fin. Code ch. 304 subch. B accrues at the postjudgment rate in effect at the time of judgment (Fin. Code 304.003 rate = Fed prime on the 15th of prior month, floor 5%, cap 15%), mirroring Fin. Code 304.103-.104.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Earlier of (a) 180th day after defendant receives written notice of the claim or (b) date suit is filed; ends day before judgment (Kenneco, adopting Fin. Code 304.104 rule for common-law claims).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Johnson & Higgins of Tex., Inc. v. Kenneco Energy, Inc., 962 S.W.2d 507 (Tex. 1998); Tex. Fin. Code 304.003, 304.103, 304.104; see also Tex. Fin. Code 302.002

postjudgmentInterest.formula: If the contract provides for interest: lesser of the contract rate (may be variable) or 18%/yr (Fin. Code 304.002). Otherwise: prime rate published by the Federal Reserve Board as determined by the Consumer Credit Commissioner on the 15th of each month for judgments rendered the following month, floor 5%, cap 15% (304.003). Accrues from rendition to satisfaction (304.005); compounds annually (304.006).

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 38.001(b)(8): a person may recover reasonable attorney's fees, in addition to the amount of a valid claim and costs, on a claim for an oral or written contract, from an individual or 'organization' (as defined in Bus. Orgs. Code 1.002) other than a quasi-governmental entity authorized by state law, a religious organization, a charitable organization, or a charitable trust (as amended by H.B. 1578, eff. Sept. 1, 2021 - replaced the former 'individual or corporation' language). Procedure (38.002): claimant must be represented by an attorney, must present the claim to the opposing party, and payment of the just amount owed must not have been tendered within 30 days of presentment. Usual and customary fees presumed reasonable (38.003). Chapter liberally construed (38.005); does not apply to certain insurance contracts (38.006).
feeShifting.citation: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 38.001-38.006

deficiency.fmvLimit: Nonjudicial (power-of-sale under Prop. Code 51.002): any person against whom deficiency is sought may by motion ask the court to determine FMV at the foreclosure-sale date; if FMV exceeds sale price, offset = FMV (less unextinguished liens) minus sale price; if no request or no competent evidence, sale price is used (51.003(b)-(c)). Judicial foreclosure: any obligor incl. guarantor may sue in the county where the property lies for an FMV determination and the same offset (51.004). Guarantor with a prior judgment against it: 51.005 FMV suit.
deficiency.timeLimit: Nonjudicial sale: deficiency action must be brought within 2 years of the foreclosure sale (51.003(a)). Judicial sale: obligor's FMV-offset suit must be brought within 90 days after the sale (guarantor without actual notice: 90 days after actual notice) (51.004(b)); 51.005 guarantor suit: 90 days after the later of the sale or actual notice.

secondReading.notes: Current rate: OCCC Historical Table of Postjudgment Interest Rates (Rev. 9/17/2026) lists 6.75% for judgments rendered in each month Jan-Oct 2026 (Oct 2026 rate set 9/15/2026); source https://occc.texas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/PostjudgmentInterestRate_History.pdf. Because common-law prejudgment interest uses the postjudgment rate at the time of judgment, it is the same 304.003 rate (a contract-rate postjudgment figure under 304.002 is not verified as the prejudgment rate). Kenneco was an insurance-broker negligence case, but its holding expressly states that where the statute does not apply, prejudgment interest is governed by the common law and it adopted the statutory rate/accrual/simple-interest rules for common-law claims; the Kenneco holding was read via FindLaw's copy of the opinion (decided Jan. 16, 1998). contractRateControls left null: Fin. Code 304.002 verifies that a contract rate (capped at 18%) controls POSTjudgment interest; that a lease/note rate displaces the common-law prejudgment rate is a contract-damages principle I did not verify from a statute or a read opinion. Related: Fin. Code 302.002 allows 6%/yr legal interest on credit extended beginning the 30th day after due where the creditor has not agreed with the obligor to charge interest (an account-type rule; its interplay with Kenneco not verified). Fees: no Texas statute makes a one-sided contractual fee clause reciprocal (no statute found; Texas enforces fee clauses as written). 38.001 fees are statutory and do not depend on a fee clause. Pointer corrections: 304.003 floor/cap and 304.002 lesser-of-contract-or-18% confirmed; ADDED: 304.006 postjudgment interest compounds annually; 51.003's 2-year limit applies to nonjudicial sales under 51.002 only, judicial foreclosures governed by 51.004 (90-day FMV suit). 38.001 as amended 2021 now reaches LLCs/partnerships as 'organizations' (Bus. Orgs. Code 1.002) except the listed quasi-governmental/religious/charitable entities.

resolutions: contract claims take the post-judgment rate at the time of judgment (Johnson & Higgins v. Kenneco, 962 S.W.2d 507); 2026 rate 6.75% per the OCCC table (Fin. Code 304.003)

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 10% per annum legal rate for a contract, 'including ... a loan or forbearance of any money ... or a claim for breach of contract', unless the parties expressly specify a different rate (15-1-1(2)). Available on common-law standard: 'where the damage is complete, the amount of the loss is fixed as of a particular time, and the loss is measurable by facts and figures' (Encon, quoting Bjork); not barred because the calculation method is disputed or figures changed, but unavailable where damages rest in the fact-finder's discretion.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time the loss is fixed (the date the damage is complete and the amount ascertainable) -- e.g., each installment of rent as it falls due (Bjork/Encon standard; exact accrual date is a case-law application, not a statutory rule).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Utah Code 15-1-1; Encon Utah, LLC v. Fluor Ames Kraemer, LLC, 2009 UT 7, 210 P.3d 263, paras. 51-55; Bjork v. April Indus., Inc., 560 P.2d 315 (Utah 1977)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment on a lawful contract: the interest rate agreed by the parties, specified in the judgment (15-1-4(2)(a)). All other civil judgments: federal postjudgment interest rate (28 U.S.C. 1961) as of January 1 of each year, plus 2%; the rate in effect at judgment stays fixed for the life of the judgment (15-1-4(3)). Judgment under $10,000 in an action regarding purchase of goods and services: 10% plus the federal postjudgment rate in effect on January 1 of the judgment year (15-1-4(4)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Utah Code 15-1-4 (as amended 2026 Gen. Sess. ch. 38)

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: Utah Code 78B-5-826: a court 'may' award costs and attorney fees to either party that prevails in a civil action based on a promissory note, written contract, or other writing executed after April 28, 1986, when the writing allows at least one party to recover attorney fees (discretionary).
feeShifting.citation: Utah Code 78B-5-826

deficiency.fmvLimit: After a trustee's sale, the complaint must plead the debt, sale price, and fair market value at the sale date; the court must find FMV and may not render judgment for more than the amount by which the debt with interest, costs, and expenses of sale (including trustee's and attorney fees) exceeds FMV as of the sale date. Prevailing party in the deficiency action recovers costs and reasonable attorney fees.
deficiency.timeLimit: Action must be commenced within three months after the trustee's sale.
deficiency.citation: Utah Code 57-1-32

UT.notes: Prejudgment interest compounding left null: 15-1-1 sets the rate but does not state simple vs. compound, and I did not find a source stating the rule for contract claims; courts' practice is not verified here. Accrual date is case-law (Bjork/Encon), stated generally. Deficiency entry covers trust-deed (nonjudicial) sales only; judicial mortgage foreclosure deficiency rules (Title 78B, ch. 6, pt. 9) not researched. 15-1-4 was amended in the 2026 General Session (ch. 38); current text read from le.utah.gov.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time the damage is complete and the amount of loss is fixed and measurable by facts and figures (e.g., each rent/loan installment's due date), not from judgment (Bjork v. April Indus., 560 P.2d 315, 317 (Utah 1977), as applied in Kraatz v. Heritage Imports, 2003 UT App 201).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Utah Code 15-1-1(1)-(2); Bjork v. April Indus., Inc., 560 P.2d 315, 317 (Utah 1977); Kraatz v. Heritage Imports, 2003 UT App 201, paras. 64-75

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment on a lawful contract conforms to the contract and bears the interest agreed by the parties, specified in the judgment (15-1-4(2)(a)). Otherwise: federal postjudgment interest rate (28 U.S.C. 1961) as of January 1 of each year plus 2%, fixed for the life of the judgment (15-1-4(3)). Judgments under $10,000 in an action regarding purchase of goods and services: 10% plus the Jan. 1 federal rate (15-1-4(4)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Utah Code 15-1-4 (eff. 3/13/2026, amended by ch. 38, 2026 Gen. Sess.)

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: Utah Code 78B-5-826: a court MAY award costs and attorney fees to either party that prevails in a civil action based on a promissory note, written contract, or other writing executed after April 28, 1986, when the writing allows at least one party to recover attorney fees (discretionary reciprocity).
feeShifting.citation: Utah Code 78B-5-826

deficiency.fmvLimit: Trustee's sale: complaint must state the debt, sale price and fair market value at the sale date; the court must find FMV and may not render judgment for more than the amount by which the debt with interest, costs and expenses of sale (incl. trustee's and attorney fees) exceeds FMV at the date of sale; prevailing party in the deficiency action recovers costs and reasonable attorney fees (57-1-32). Judicial mortgage foreclosure: if sale proceeds are insufficient, the judgment for the balance is docketed and execution may issue (78B-6-902); no FMV limit found in that statute.
deficiency.timeLimit: Trustee's sale: action must be commenced within three months after the sale (57-1-32). Judicial foreclosure: deficiency is part of the one foreclosure action (78B-6-901, -902); no separate statutory deadline found.

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest is not a separate statute for contract claims; availability is by case law (loss fixed at a particular time and measurable by facts and figures; a dispute over valuation method or conflicting testimony does not by itself defeat it, per Kraatz paras. 64-71, read from Justia's copy of the opinion). Rate: 15-1-1(2) sets the legal rate for 'a claim for breach of contract' at 10% per annum unless the parties expressly specify a different rate; 15-1-1(1) lets parties agree any rate, so a lease/note rate controls. compounding left null: 15-1-1 and the cases read do not say; simple interest is the ordinary practice but not verified from text for contract claims (78B-5-824(5) mandates simple interest but applies only to personal-injury special damages). Current postjudgment figures published by Utah Courts (https://www.utcourts.gov/en/court-records-publications/resources/interest-rates/interestrates.html): 2026 federal rate 3.51%, 15-1-4(3)(a) rate 5.51%, 15-1-4(4) rate 13.51%, for judgments entered in calendar 2026. Fees: no general contract-claim fee statute found (Utah follows the American rule: fees only by statute or contract). 78B-5-826 reciprocity is discretionary ('may'). Pointer corrections: 78B-5-824 is personal-injury prejudgment interest only (prime+2, floor 5%, cap 10%) and does NOT govern contract claims; 78B-6-906 is the redemption/parcel-sale section, the judicial deficiency provision is 78B-6-902; 15-1-4 was amended effective 3/13/2026 (adds Business and Chancery Court to 'court') but the rate formula is unchanged.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Award and start date are discretionary: the verdict or judgment 'may provide for interest on any principal sum awarded, or any part thereof, and fix the period at which the interest shall commence' (8.01-382). Rate: if the contract does not fix an interest rate, the court 'shall apply the judgment rate of six percent to calculate prejudgment interest pursuant to § 8.01-382' (6.2-302(B)); a judgment in an action arising from a contract carries the contract rate or 6%, whichever is higher (6.2-302(A)). Judgment on a negotiable instrument must carry interest at the rate specified in the instrument, else the 6% judgment rate (8.01-382).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Fixed by the fact-finder / court in its discretion ('fix the period at which the interest shall commence'); no statutory default start date.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Va. Code 8.01-382; Va. Code 6.2-302

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 6% per annum; a money judgment in an action arising from a contract carries the rate lawfully charged on the contract or 6%, whichever is higher (6.2-302(A)). Rate in effect at entry of judgment governs for the life of the judgment (6.2-302(C)). If the judgment does not provide for interest, it bears the 6.2-302 judgment rate from entry (8.01-382).

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (American rule; fees only by specific contract or statutory provision)

deficiency.timeLimit: No foreclosure-specific deadline found. A deficiency claim is an action on the debt, governed by general limitations: 6 years after the due date or accelerated due date for a note payable at a definite time (8.3A-118(a)); 5 years for other signed written contracts (8.01-246(A)(2)).
deficiency.citation: Va. Code 8.3A-118; 8.01-246 (no anti-deficiency or fair-value provision in Va. Code tit. 55.1, ch. 3, Deeds of Trust)

VA.notes: Prejudgment interest compounding null: 8.01-382 and 6.2-302 do not state simple vs. compound, and no Virginia authority on the point was verified here. rate 6.0 is the default when the contract fixes no rate; when the lease or note fixes a rate, 6.2-302 applies the contract rate (for the postjudgment period, the higher of contract rate or 6%). feeShifting: no Virginia statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract fee statute, was found; Virginia follows the American rule, with fee clauses enforced as written (not separately source-verified). Deficiency: allowed=true is based on the absence of any anti-deficiency or fair-market-value provision in Va. Code tit. 55.1 ch. 3 (full chapter text searched for 'deficien', no hits) plus secondary sources (Nolo) stating Virginia permits deficiency judgments without statutory limits after judicial and nonjudicial foreclosure; no Virginia statute or Supreme Court opinion affirmatively stating the rule was read, so treat as medium confidence.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Rate: the contract rate if the contract/instrument fixes one; otherwise the 6% judgment rate (Va. Code 6.2-302(B)). Whether to award and the start date are set by the jury/court (8.01-382).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Date fixed by the verdict, judgment or decree in the factfinder's discretion (Va. Code 8.01-382: may 'fix the period at which the interest shall commence'). Exception: a judgment for a sum due under a negotiable instrument (e.g., a promissory note) must provide interest per 8.3A-112 at the instrument's rate.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 6% per annum, except a money judgment in an action arising from a contract carries the rate lawfully charged on the contract or 6%, whichever is higher; rate in effect at entry of judgment is fixed for that judgment (6.2-302(A),(C)). If the judgment does not provide for interest, it bears the 6.2-302 judgment rate from entry (8.01-382).

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (American rule; fees only by specific contract or statutory provision)

deficiency.timeLimit: No deficiency-specific deadline found. Deficiency is pursued as an action on the debt: 5 years for a signed written contract (Va. Code 8.01-246(A)(2)); 6 years after the stated or accelerated due date for a note payable at a definite time (8.3A-118(a)).
deficiency.citation: Va. Code 8.01-246(A)(2); 8.3A-118(a) (limitations only; no Virginia anti-deficiency or FMV statute found)

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest is discretionary by statute (8.01-382 'may provide for interest'); rate 6% unless the contract fixes a rate (6.2-302(B)), and 6.2-301(B) implies the 6% legal rate only where there is no express contract rate. 6.2-301(C): sellers of goods/services on open account without a written credit agreement may collect the 6% legal rate beginning the day after 60 days from mailing/presentation of the invoice. Leading case on the discretion not separately verified; statute text alone establishes it. compounding null: statutes read are silent on simple vs. compound and I did not verify case law. Postjudgment: 6.2-302(A) makes the contract rate carry into a contract judgment if higher than 6%. Fees: no Virginia statute makes a one-sided fee clause reciprocal and no general contract-claim fee statute was found (searched; Virginia follows the American rule and enforces fee clauses as written, per secondary sources only). Deficiency: no statute bars or limits deficiency after judicial or trustee's (nonjudicial) sale; no FMV offset statute found (Title 55.1 ch. 3 art. 2 trustee's-sale sections 55.1-320 to -325 contain no deficiency provision). This 'none found' conclusion rests on reading those sections plus secondary sources (Nolo) stating Virginia has no anti-deficiency law; fmvLimit therefore null. Pointer correction: 55.1-321 concerns pre-sale notices, not deficiency; 6.2-302 (not 6.2-301 alone) also governs the prejudgment rate via subsection (B).

resolutions: award and start date are discretionary (Va. Code 8.01-382); 6% applies when awarded and the contract sets no rate (6.2-302(B))

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Statutory legal rate: 'Except as specifically provided by law, the rate of interest or the sum allowed for forbearance or use of money shall be 12 percent per annum computed by the actuarial method' (9 V.S.A. 41a(a)). Prejudgment interest is awarded as of right when the principal sum is liquidated or capable of ready ascertainment, and is discretionary when damages are unliquidated (Remes, citing Estate of Fleming v. Nicholson, 168 Vt. 495 (1998), and Smith v. Osmun, 165 Vt. 545 (1996)); V.R.C.P. 54(a) directs that the judgment include all interest accrued up to entry of judgment.
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date the sum became due / the breach: in contract cases 'damages are to be measured at the time of breach with interest to the date of judgment' (Remes, quoting Winey v. William E. Dailey, Inc., 161 Vt. 129 (1993)).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 9 V.S.A. 41a(a); V.R.C.P. 54(a); Remes v. Nordic Group, Inc. (Vt. 1999) (https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/vt-supreme-court/1340642.html); Estate of Fleming v. Nicholson, 168 Vt. 495 (1998)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 12% per annum general statutory interest on judgments under 9 V.S.A. 41a(a); V.R.C.P. 69 directs the clerk to state post-judgment interest per day on the writ of execution 'at the maximum rate allowed by law' (Dorr v. Lacoste, Vt. Super. Ct. No. 14-1-11 Bncv (Feb. 5, 2016)). A recorded judgment lien also accrues interest at 12% (12 V.S.A. 2903(c)).

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: None for contract claims generally. Construction-contract payment claims only: Vermont Prompt Pay Act, 9 V.S.A. 4007(c) - notwithstanding any contrary agreement, the substantially prevailing party in a proceeding to recover payment within the chapter is awarded reasonable attorney's fees and expenses (and 4007(b) adds a 1%/month penalty on sums wrongfully withheld). Mortgage foreclosure: where the mortgage obligates the mortgagor to pay foreclosure attorney's fees and they are claimed in the complaint, the court allows such fee 'as in its judgment is just' (12 V.S.A. 4937, amended 2025).
feeShifting.citation: 12 V.S.A. 4937 (mortgage foreclosure only)

deficiency.timeLimit: Judicial sale: the plaintiff must request the deficiency in the foreclosure complaint and before the confirmation order issues; failure to request is deemed a waiver of any deficiency against the mortgagor (12 V.S.A. 4954(d)). Nonjudicial sale (available only for property other than farmland or a dwelling house owned by a natural person, 12 V.S.A. 4961): the statute 'shall not preclude the mortgagee from maintaining a subsequent action against the mortgagor for any deficiency' (4966(f)); no special deadline stated in that section.

VT.notes: Compounding: 41a(a) says 'computed by the actuarial method'; Remes computed prejudgment interest as a flat per-day figure, i.e., simple interest on the principal; 'actuarial method' was not separately defined in the sources read. contractRateControls null: whether a contract rate in a lease or note displaces the 12% prejudgment rate was not verified from a Vermont source (41a(a) applies 'except as specifically provided by law'). Postjudgment 12% is sourced to a Superior Court decision applying 41a(a) and V.R.C.P. 69, not a Supreme Court holding. feeShifting: no Vermont statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract fee statute, was found (American rule; fee clauses enforced as written); 12 V.S.A. 4937 only requires the court to allow a just fee in a foreclosure where the mortgage provides for fees. Deficiency: no fair-market-value offset statute found. Strict foreclosure (12 V.S.A. 4941) requires a finding of no substantial value in excess of the debt before a decree without sale; deficiency after strict foreclosure was not researched.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: As of right on liquidated or readily ascertainable sums, generally from when each sum became due (Remes: interest assessed on damages 'as they become due'); for unliquidated damages the award and its start date are in the court's discretion.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: 9 V.S.A. 41a(a) (12% legal rate); Remes v. Nordic Group, Inc., 1999 VT 9

postjudgmentInterest.citation: 9 V.S.A. 41a(a) (legal rate of 12% per annum, applied as the general statutory interest on judgments); V.R.C.P. 69 (writ of execution states per-day post-judgment interest 'at the maximum rate allowed by law'); 12 V.S.A. 2903(c) (interest on a judgment lien accrues at 12% per annum)

feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: None for contract claims generally. Construction-contract payment claims only: Vermont Prompt Pay Act, 9 V.S.A. 4007(c) - notwithstanding any contrary agreement, the substantially prevailing party in a proceeding to recover payment within the chapter is awarded reasonable attorney's fees and expenses (and 4007(b) adds a 1%/month penalty on sums wrongfully withheld). Mortgage foreclosure: where the mortgage obligates the mortgagor to pay foreclosure attorney's fees and they are claimed in the complaint, the court allows such fee 'as in its judgment is just' (12 V.S.A. 4937, amended 2025).

deficiency.timeLimit: Judicial sale: deficiency must be requested (may be in the foreclosure complaint) before the confirmation order issues; failure to request is deemed a waiver of any deficiency judgment against the mortgagor (12 V.S.A. 4954(d)). Nonjudicial sale: the sale 'shall not preclude the mortgagee from maintaining a subsequent action against the mortgagor for any deficiency' (12 V.S.A. 4966(f)); no chapter-specific deadline found.

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest availability is case law: Remes v. Nordic Group (1999 VT 9, read via FindLaw) holds interest is a matter of right when the amount is liquidated or capable of ready ascertainment, otherwise discretionary, and applied the 9 V.S.A. 41a(a) 12% rate. 41a(a) says 12% 'computed by the actuarial method'; compounding left null because I did not verify whether Vermont courts treat prejudgment/judgment interest as simple (the actuarial-method definition in 41a(d) concerns allocation of loan payments). contractRateControls null: whether a lease/note rate displaces the 12% prejudgment rate was not verified from a statute or a read opinion. Postjudgment: no stand-alone judgment-interest statute found; courts apply 41a(a)'s 12% (see Dorr v. Lacoste, No. 14-1-11 Bncv (Vt. Super. Ct. Feb. 5, 2016), vermontjudiciary.org/media/990, describing 41a(a) as 'the general statutory interest on judgments'); 12 V.S.A. 2903(c) sets 12% on judgment liens; whether a contract rate carries into the judgment not verified. Nonjudicial power of sale (12 V.S.A. 4961) is available for any property except farmland or a dwelling house owned by a natural person, so it is available for commercial property. Strict foreclosure (4941) requires a finding of no substantial equity; 4941 contains no deficiency provision and deficiency after strict foreclosure was not verified. fmvLimit null: no statutory fair-market-value offset found in chapter 172. Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract-fee statute found (American rule). Pointer corrections: 12 V.S.A. 2903 is the judgment-LIEN duration section (its subsection (c) sets 12% on judgment liens), not a general judgment-interest statute; the Vermont deficiency provisions are 12 V.S.A. 4954(d) (judicial sale) and 4966(f) (nonjudicial), not 4943; the official 41a history note shows no amendment after 1995, No. 162 (a search-result claim of a 2025 amendment was not borne out by the official text).

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Liquidated claims only: a claim is liquidated 'where the evidence furnishes data which, if believed, makes it possible to compute the amount with exactness, without reliance on opinion or discretion' (Hill, quoting Hansen v. Rothaus and Prier v. Refrigeration Eng'g Co.). Rate: 12% per annum under RCW 19.52.010(1) ('every loan or forbearance of money ... shall bear interest at the rate of twelve percent per annum where no different rate is agreed to in writing'); Washington courts treat a liquidated claim 'as if it were a loan made to the defendant' (Hill).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date each liquidated sum became due (breach/due date); available only if the claim is liquidated or determinable by computation from a fixed standard in the contract without opinion or discretion (Prier).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: RCW 19.52.010(1); Hill v. Garda CL Nw., Inc., 191 Wn.2d 553, 424 P.3d 207 (2018); Hansen v. Rothaus, 107 Wn.2d 468, 472-73, 730 P.2d 662 (1986); Prier v. Refrigeration Eng'g Co., 74 Wn.2d 25, 32-34, 442 P.2d 621 (1968)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment founded on a written contract providing for interest until paid at a specified rate: the contract rate, if set forth in the judgment (RCW 4.56.110(1)). Otherwise (non-tort, non-consumer): from entry at the maximum rate permitted under RCW 19.52.020 on the date of entry = the higher of 12% or 4 percentage points above the equivalent coupon issue yield of the average 26-week Treasury bill rate at the first auction of the preceding calendar month (RCW 4.56.110(6); 19.52.020(1)). Tort judgments: prime + 2 (4.56.110(3)(b)); consumer-debt judgments: 9% (4.56.110(5)).

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: RCW 4.84.330: in any action on a contract or lease entered into after Sept. 21, 1977 that provides for fees to one of the parties, the prevailing party (the party in whose favor final judgment is rendered), whether or not the party named in the clause, 'shall be entitled to reasonable attorneys' fees'; the right cannot be waived and any waiver provision is void (mandatory).
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: RCW 4.84.250-.280: prevailing-party fees in actions for damages where the amount pleaded is $10,000 or less (small-claim threshold, not a general contract fee statute).

deficiency.fmvLimit: After a nonjudicial trustee's sale: no deficiency against any borrower, grantor, or guarantor except as permitted for commercial loans (61.24.100(1)). For a deed of trust securing a commercial loan executed after June 11, 1998: (a) against the borrower/grantor, only for decrease in fair value caused by waste and for wrongfully retained rents, insurance proceeds, or condemnation awards, and only to the extent fair value of property sold to the beneficiary or an affiliate is less than the debt (61.24.100(3)(a)); (b) against a guarantor given timely notice, the deficiency equals the amount owed less the GREATER of fair value or the sale price, plus contract interest from the sale date and contractual costs and fees (61.24.100(3)(c), (5)). A lender that forecloses the deed of trust judicially as a mortgage is outside 61.24.100 (61.24.100(8)); judicial-foreclosure deficiency rules (RCW 61.12) not researched.
deficiency.timeLimit: Actions under 61.24.100(3)(a) and (c) must be commenced within one year after the trustee's sale (or the last sale, if more than one), or a later date agreed in writing after notice of foreclosure, plus any period the action is stayed by bankruptcy or similar law (61.24.100(4)).

WA.notes: Prejudgment compounding and accrual start left null: the sources read establish the liquidated-claim test and 12% rate but I did not read a Washington holding stating simple vs. compound or the default accrual date for contract claims (commonly the date each sum became due, but not verified here). contractRateControls=true rests on RCW 19.52.010's text ('where no different rate is agreed to in writing'). RCW 19.52.010(3) excludes certain consumer leases from 'loan or forbearance'; commercial leases are not addressed by that subsection. Commercial-loan borrower deficiency after a trustee's sale is sharply limited (waste and misappropriated rents etc.); guarantor deficiency is the main recovery route. Not covered: RCW 4.84.250 (fees in small claims of $10,000 or less).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the date each liquidated sum became due (breach/due date); available only if the claim is liquidated or determinable by computation from a fixed standard in the contract without opinion or discretion (Prier).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: RCW 19.52.010(1) (12% per annum 'where no different rate is agreed to in writing'); Prier v. Refrigeration Eng'g Co., 74 Wn.2d 25, 442 P.2d 621 (1968) (liquidated-claim test); Caruso v. Local Union No. 690, 50 Wn. App. 688 (1988) (compound interest never implied)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Judgment on a written contract providing for interest until paid at a specified rate bears the contract rate if that rate is set forth in the judgment (RCW 4.56.110(1)); otherwise the maximum rate under RCW 19.52.020 on the date of entry = higher of 12% or 4 points above the 26-week T-bill coupon-equivalent yield from the first auction of the preceding month (computed monthly by the State Treasurer, published in the Washington State Register). 12.00% for every month of 2026 published through September 2026.

feeShifting.reciprocalStatute: RCW 4.84.330: in an action on a contract or lease entered after Sept. 21, 1977 whose fee provision awards fees to one party or the prevailing party, the prevailing party (the party in whose favor final judgment is rendered) recovers reasonable fees and costs whether or not it is the party named in the clause; the right cannot be waived and any waiver is void.
feeShifting.generalContractFeeStatute: RCW 4.84.250-.280: prevailing-party fees in actions for damages where the amount pleaded is $10,000 or less (small-claim threshold, not a general contract fee statute).

deficiency.allowed: Judicial foreclosure (ch. 61.12 RCW): allowed, but no deficiency if the court-found fair value applied to the debt discharges it. Nonjudicial trustee's sale under a deed of trust (ch. 61.24 RCW): generally barred against borrower, grantor and guarantor; for commercial loans (deeds of trust not on a principal residence) executed after June 11, 1998, a deficiency may be sought against the borrower/grantor only for waste or wrongful retention of rents/insurance/condemnation proceeds, and against a guarantor subject to statutory conditions.
deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial: RCW 61.12.060 fair value found by the court applied to the debt; no deficiency if it discharges the debt. Trustee's sale guarantor action: guarantor may ask the court to determine fair value of the property; deficiency is measured against the greater of fair value or the sale price (RCW 61.24.100(5)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Trustee's sale: action against borrower (waste/retention) or guarantor must be commenced within one year after the trustee's sale, or a later date the liable party agrees to in writing (RCW 61.24.100(4)). Judicial: deficiency is part of the foreclosure decree; no separate limit identified.

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest on a liquidated contract claim is a matter of right under Prier (case law, not a specific statute); the 12% default rate of RCW 19.52.010 applies where no different rate is agreed in writing, so a written lease/note rate controls (subject to usury limits in ch. 19.52 RCW; commercial-loan usury exemptions were not researched here). Unliquidated claims do not earn prejudgment interest. Simple interest per Caruso (compounding only if expressly agreed); Caruso was located via search snippet and not read in full. Post-judgment 'rate' left null because it is a formula (contract rate or RCW 19.52.020 max rate); current value 12.00% for Jan-Sept 2026 per the Treasurer's rates published by the Code Reviser (https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/Law/CRO/WSRhtm/rates.htm). RCW 4.56.110(3) (tort judgments: prime + 2) does not apply to contract claims. Pointer check: all WA pointers confirmed.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Legal rate: 'The rate of interest upon the loan or forbearance of any money, goods or things in action shall be $5 upon the $100 for one year' (5% per year), unless the parties contract in writing for a different lawful rate (138.04). Recoverable on a liquidated claim (Estreen v. Bluhm annotation to 138.04). Separately, a statutory settlement offer that the offeror beats at judgment earns interest at 1% + prime (Jan. 1 or July 1 H.15 rate of the judgment year) from the date of the offer until paid, in lieu of 814.04(4)/815.05(8) interest (807.01(4)).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: 'A creditor is entitled to interest on a liquidated claim from the time payment was due by the terms of the contract and, if no time is specified, then from the time demand was made or from commencement of the action' (Estreen v. Bluhm, 79 Wis. 2d 142 (1977), as annotated to 138.04). Interest from verdict/decision to entry of judgment at 1% + prime is added to costs (814.04(4)).

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 1% plus the prime rate reported in Federal Reserve statistical release H.15, in effect on January 1 of the judgment year (judgments entered Jan. 1-June 30) or July 1 (judgments entered after June 30), from entry of judgment until paid (815.05(8)); same rate from verdict/decision to entry of judgment (814.04(4)); 807.01(4) settlement-offer interest displaces both where applicable.

feeShifting.citation: Wis. Stat. 814.045(2)-(3) (fee-reasonableness statute: presumption that reasonable fees do not exceed 3x compensatory damages, but it 'does not abrogate' fee agreements and a fee agreement is presumed reasonable)

deficiency.fmvLimit: Judicial foreclosure only. If the premises sell for less than the debt and costs of sale, 'there is no presumption that the mortgaged premises sold for their fair value,' and the court may not confirm the sale or render a deficiency judgment until satisfied that the fair value of the premises has been credited on the mortgage debt, interest, and costs (846.16(2m)(ae)). Deficiency must be demanded in the complaint, ordered in the original judgment, and rendered against the personally liable party on or after confirmation (846.04(1)). For commercial property, the plaintiff may elect in the complaint to waive deficiency (if the mortgagor agreed in writing), which shortens the sale wait from 6 months to 3 months after judgment (846.103).
deficiency.timeLimit: No separate post-sale deadline: the deficiency must be demanded in the foreclosure complaint and is rendered on or after confirmation of sale (846.04(1)).

WI.notes: Compounding 'simple' rests on 138.04's wording ('$5 upon the $100 for one year and according to that rate for a greater or less sum or for a longer or a shorter time'); no case on compounding was read. The Estreen accrual rule is quoted from the Legislature's own annotation to 138.04. feeShifting: no Wisconsin statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract fee statute, was found (American rule; fee clauses enforced as written; not separately source-verified). Wisconsin mortgage foreclosure is judicial; the deficiency must be pleaded in the foreclosure action itself.

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From the time payment was due under the contract; if no time is specified, from demand or commencement of the action (Estreen v. Bluhm, 79 Wis. 2d 142, 255 N.W.2d 473 (1977), as annotated to s. 138.04). Common-law availability requires damages that are liquidated or determinable by an objective standard.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Wis. Stat. 138.04 ($5 per $100 per year unless a different rate is clearly expressed in writing); Murray v. Holiday Rambler, Inc., 83 Wis. 2d 406, 438-39 (1978) and Singler v. Zurich Am. Ins. Co., 2014 WI App 108 (5% legal rate applies to prejudgment interest absent a contract rate); Wis. Stat. 807.01(4) (offer-of-settlement interest)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 1 percentage point plus the prime rate (Federal Reserve H.15) in effect on January 1 of the year of entry if judgment entered on or before June 30, or on July 1 if entered after June 30; fixed from entry until paid. No statutory provision for a contract rate to carry into the judgment. Per the Wisconsin court system's published table: 7.75% for Jan 1-Jun 30, 2026 and 7.75% for Jul 1-Dec 31, 2026 (8.5% for 2025).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: Wis. Stat. 815.05(8); Wisconsin Court System, Interest Rates on Civil Judgments (2011-2026)

feeShifting.citation: Wis. Stat. 814.045(2)-(3) (fee-reasonableness statute: presumption that reasonable fees do not exceed 3x compensatory damages, but it 'does not abrogate' fee agreements and a fee agreement is presumed reasonable)

deficiency.allowed: Allowed in judicial foreclosure against every party personally liable for the mortgage debt, if demanded in the complaint (s. 846.04(1)). For commercial property the plaintiff may instead elect in the complaint to waive deficiency (only if the mortgagor agreed in writing at execution), which shortens the post-judgment sale delay from 6 months to 3 months (s. 846.103).
deficiency.fmvLimit: Court may not confirm the sale or render a deficiency judgment unless satisfied that fair value of the premises has been credited to the debt; no presumption that a below-debt sale price is fair value (s. 846.16(2m)(ae)).
deficiency.timeLimit: Deficiency must be demanded in the foreclosure complaint and is determined at confirmation of sale (5 days' notice stating the personal judgment sought, s. 846.165). A 10-year limit applies only to agricultural property (s. 846.04(2)).

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest on liquidated/determinable contract damages is common law, at the 5% s. 138.04 legal rate unless the contract clearly states a different rate in writing; unliquidated claims generally do not earn it. Compounding left null: no Wisconsin authority on simple vs compound for common-law prejudgment interest was read (5% 'per year' wording suggests simple, not verified). Separately, s. 807.01(4): if a plaintiff's rejected statutory settlement offer is equaled or beaten, interest at 1% + prime (same Jan 1/Jul 1 setting as 815.05(8); 7.75% for 2026) runs on the amount recovered from the date of the offer until paid. Post-judgment rate is a formula (null number); 2026 = 7.75% both halves. Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract fee statute found; contractual fee clauses are enforceable and presumed reasonable under 814.045(3). The pointer's '846.101/846.103 waiver of deficiency shortens redemption' is partly right: 846.101 covers owner-occupied 1-4 family, farm, church and tax-exempt nonprofit property; 846.103 covers commercial and multifamily property (6-month vs 3-month sale delay, not a 'redemption' period). The pointer's '846.165 FMV at confirmation' is corrected: the fair-value rule is in 846.16(2m)(ae); 846.165 is the confirmation-notice section. Whether any nonjudicial (advertisement) foreclosure route exists for commercial mortgages was not verified; ch. 846 judicial foreclosure is the rule analyzed here.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Court 'may award prejudgment interest on all or some of the amount of the special or liquidated damages, as calculated after the amount of any settlements' (56-6-31(b)). Rate: two percentage points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year in which the right to bring the action accrued; floor 4%, cap 9%; the rate stays fixed until judgment; the Supreme Court of Appeals' administrative office publishes the rate annually (56-6-31(b)(1)). Cases accruing before 2009: the rate in effect January 2 of the accrual year (56-6-31(b)(2)). If the obligation is based on a written agreement, it bears prejudgment interest 'at the rate and terms set forth in the written agreement' until judgment. Separately, in any action founded on contract the jury 'may allow interest on the principal due' (56-6-27).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Statute fixes the RATE by the year the right to bring the action accrued; it does not state the start date of accrual. Start date not verified (see notes).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: W. Va. Code 56-6-31(a)-(b); W. Va. Code 56-6-27

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Two percentage points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year the judgment is entered; floor 4%, cap 9%; fixed for the life of the judgment; simple, not compounding (56-6-31(a), (c)). Where the obligation is on a written agreement, the contract rate applies only until judgment, and after that the 56-6-31(c) judgment rate applies (56-6-31(b)).

feeShifting.citation: No statute found

deficiency.fmvLimit: No fair-market-value limit: a grantor, obligor, maker, comaker, guarantor, surety, or other defendant in a deficiency action 'may not assert as a defense that the fair market value of secured real property was not obtained at a trust deed foreclosure sale conducted in accordance with this article' (38-1-7(b)). Sale proceeds are applied to expenses, trustee commission, then the secured debts, with surplus to the grantor (38-1-7(a)).
deficiency.citation: W. Va. Code 38-1-7

WV.notes: Prejudgment interest is discretionary ('may award') even on liquidated damages; the calculator should treat it as available but not automatic. The applicable rate depends on the accrual year and must be read from the Supreme Court of Appeals' annual published rate (not fetched here). Accrual start date left unverified: 56-6-31 sets the rate by the year the cause of action accrued but does not say from which date interest runs; case law on the start date for contract claims was not read. feeShifting: no West Virginia statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract fee statute, was found (American rule assumed, not separately source-verified). Deficiency timeLimit null: 38-1-7 sets no deadline and the general limitations periods for an action on the note or guaranty were not verified here.

prejudgmentInterest.formula: 2 percentage points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District (Richmond) secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year in which the right to bring the action accrued, floor 4% and ceiling 9% per annum; rate fixed for that case until judgment. Determined annually by the Administrative Office of the Supreme Court of Appeals. 6.25% for 2026 (Richmond Fed secondary rate 4.25% on Jan. 2, 2026, per the court's Jan. 2, 2026 release).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Statute keys the rate to the year the right to bring the action accrued (as determined by the court); it does not otherwise state a start date. For obligations under a written agreement, interest runs per the agreement's own rate and terms until judgment.

postjudgmentInterest.formula: Simple interest at 2 points above the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate in effect on January 2 of the year the judgment is entered, floor 4%, ceiling 9%; 6.25% for judgments entered in calendar 2026. A written-agreement contract rate applies only until judgment; after judgment the statutory rate applies (56-6-31(b)).
postjudgmentInterest.citation: W. Va. Code 56-6-31(a)-(c); Supreme Court of Appeals of W. Va. Administrative Office release, Jan. 2, 2026

feeShifting.citation: No statute found

deficiency.citation: W. Va. Code 38-1-7(b)

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest: 56-6-31(b) says the court 'may' award prejudgment interest on special or liquidated damages (so availability is discretionary), but the rate is the statutory formula, not court-set; 'notwithstanding' the 6% legal rate of W. Va. Code 47-6-5(a) (pointer's 47-6-5 6% is correct but displaced by 56-6-31 for prejudgment interest). For a written-agreement obligation the contract rate and terms govern until judgment; statutory rate after. The prejudgment rate for a given case is the rate for the year the claim accrued, so a 2026 figure (6.25%) applies only to claims accruing in 2026; earlier years' rates are on the court's site (not collected here). Pointer said 'prime rate + 2'; the statute actually uses the Fifth Federal Reserve District secondary discount rate + 2 (floor 4, ceiling 9) - corrected. Fees: no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract fee statute found after searching (American rule; contractual fee clauses governed by case law, not researched to a leading case). Deficiency: no anti-deficiency statute found; deeds of trust are foreclosed by trustee's sale (ch. 38, art. 1) and 38-1-7(b) (2015, abrogating Sostaric v. Marshall, 234 W. Va. 449 (2014)) bars any defendant, including guarantors, from defending a deficiency action on the ground that fair market value was not obtained at a trustee's sale conducted per the article; so fmvLimit null. No deficiency-specific time limit found; ordinary limitations period on the debt instrument applies (not researched), so timeLimit null.

resolutions: award is discretionary ('may', W. Va. Code 56-6-31(b)); 2026 formula rate 6.25%

prejudgmentInterest.formula: Two-part test: '(1) the claim must be liquidated, as opposed to unliquidated, meaning it is readily computable via simple mathematics; and (2) the debtor must receive notice of the amount due before interest begins to accumulate.' Rate: 'in the absence of a contractual agreement to a different percentage, the appropriate measure of prejudgment interest is the seven percent per annum stated in Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-14-106(e)' (Ropken, 2025 WY 1, para. 10). Statute: 'If there is no agreement or provision of law for a different rate, the interest of money shall be at the rate of seven percent (7%) per annum' (40-14-106(e)).
prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: From notice: 'Prejudgment interest generally is computed from the time notice is given of the claim' (Ropken, para. 29); e.g., a demand letter stating the amount due.
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Wyo. Stat. 40-14-106(e); Ropken v. YJ Construction, Inc., 2025 WY 1, paras. 10, 29

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 10% per year from rendition until paid (1-16-102(a)); if the judgment is founded on a contract in which all parties agreed to interest at a certain rate, the judgment rate 'shall correspond to the terms of the contract' (1-16-102(b)).

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (Wyo. Stat. Title 1 searched); Wyo. Stat. 1-14-126(b) only sets factors where fees are otherwise authorized; Wyo. Stat. 34-4-112 limits contractual fees added in foreclosure by advertisement

deficiency.citation: Wyo. Stat. 34-4-113(c) (foreclosure by advertisement and sale): 'a mortgagee shall account to and pay a mortgagor for any surplus, and the mortgagor is liable for any deficiency'

WY.notes: Prejudgment compounding null: Ropken describes 'simple mathematic calculations' for liquidation but does not address simple vs. compound interest; not verified. 40-14-106 sits in Wyoming's consumer credit code, but the Wyoming Supreme Court applies subsection (e)'s 7% as the general prejudgment rate (Ropken). Ropken text read via FindLaw (https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/wy-supreme-court/118020157.html). feeShifting: no Wyoming statute making one-sided contract fee clauses reciprocal, and no general contract fee statute, was found (American rule assumed, not separately source-verified); Wyo. Stat. 34-4-112 only conditions adding a mortgage's fee clause to the debt in a foreclosure by advertisement on an attorney's no-fee-splitting affidavit. Deficiency: Titles 34 and 1 were searched for 'deficiency'; no fair-market-value offset or special time limit was found, so fmvLimit and timeLimit are null (general limitations on the note or guaranty not verified).

prejudgmentInterest.accrualStart: Generally from the time the debtor receives notice of the amount due (e.g., a demand letter itemizing the unpaid sum), not from breach or verdict (Ropken v. YJ Constr., Inc., 2025 WY 131).
prejudgmentInterest.citation: Wyo. Stat. 40-14-106(e) ('If there is no agreement or provision of law for a different rate, the interest of money shall be at the rate of seven percent (7%) per annum'); Ropken v. YJ Construction, Inc., 2025 WY 131 (two-part test: claim liquidated, i.e. readily computable by simple mathematics, and debtor had notice of the amount due)

postjudgmentInterest.formula: 10% per year from rendition until paid; if the judgment is founded on a contract in which all parties agreed to interest at a certain rate, the judgment bears the contract rate instead.

feeShifting.citation: No statute found (Wyo. Stat. Title 1 searched); Wyo. Stat. 1-14-126(b) only sets factors where fees are otherwise authorized; Wyo. Stat. 34-4-112 limits contractual fees added in foreclosure by advertisement

deficiency.citation: Wyo. Stat. 34-4-113(c) ('the mortgagor is liable for any deficiency'); applies to judicial foreclosure sales via Wyo. Stat. 1-18-113 and to foreclosure by advertisement (power of sale) under ch. 34-4

secondReading.notes: Prejudgment interest: statute supplies only the 7% default rate; availability is case law (liquidated + notice test, Ropken, 2025 WY 131, read via FindLaw's copy of the opinion; interest computed from notice/demand). A contract rate displaces 7% ('if there is no agreement'). 40-14-106 sits in the Wyoming Uniform Consumer Credit Code, but subsection (e) is worded as a general legal rate and Ropken applied it to a construction contract claim. Compounding left null: no Wyoming authority on simple vs compound prejudgment interest was read. Post-judgment: 10% fixed, contract rate carries into a judgment founded on a contract with an agreed rate (1-16-102(b)); pointer's 'contract rate if lower?' is corrected - the statute is not limited to lower rates. Fees: American rule; no reciprocal-fee statute and no general contract-claim fee statute found after searching Title 1; contractual fee clauses govern. 34-4-112 conditions adding a mortgage/note fee clause to the debt in foreclosure by advertisement on an attorney affidavit of no fee-sharing. Deficiency: allowed after both judicial and advertisement foreclosure (34-4-113(c)); no fair-market-value limit and no deficiency-specific time limit found in Titles 1 or 34 (ordinary limitations period on the note applies, not researched), so fmvLimit and timeLimit null. Pointer '1-18-? / 34-4-113?' confirmed as 34-4-113(c) and 1-18-113.

resolutions: case is Ropken v. YJ Construction, 2025 WY 131 (docket S-25-0001); the second reading's '2025 WY 1' was the docket number
